reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump's use of Twitter. The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform. Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant. Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace. A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use "distributed trust" to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias. "Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints," the survey concluded. Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people's reliance on social media led to greater political engagement. Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in "misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news" via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue. "This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem," says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group. So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.

questions.stem: According to Paragraphs 1 and 2, many young Americans cast doubts on____
options: A) the justification of the news-filtering practice.
B) people's preference for social media platforms.
C) the administration's ability to handle information.
D) social media as a reliable source of news.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 D）social media as a reliable source of news. 定位句在第 1 段：其言下之意是：千禧一代更愿意白宫的新闻经由其他渠道过滤呈现，而不是来自总统的社交媒体平台。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform ↔ social media as a reliable source of news；as distrust has risen toward all media ↔ social media as a reliable source of news）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The phrase "beef up" (Line 2, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to____
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是词义句意题，正确答案 A）sharpen. 定位句在第 2 段：然而随着对所有媒体的不信任上升，人们或许正开始强化自身的媒介素养能力。正确项与原文构成同义替换（beef up their media literacy skills ↔ sharpen）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to the Knight Foundation survey, young people____
options: A) tend to voice their opinions in cyberspace.
B) verify news by referring to diverse sources.
C) have a strong sense of responsibility.
D) like to exchange views on "distributed trust".
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 B）verify news by referring to diverse sources. 定位句在第 3 段：他们交叉核对来源，并偏好来自不同视角的新闻——尤其是那些坦诚承认自身偏见的来源。正确项与原文构成同义替换（They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives ↔ verify news by referring to diverse sources；they use "distributed trust" to verify stories ↔ verify news by referring to diverse sources）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The Barna survey found that a main cause for the fake news problem is____
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 C）readers' misinterpretation. 定位句在第 5 段：Barna 调查机构的一项调查发现，美国人为"假新闻现象"列出的首要原因是"读者错误"，其权重高于编造的新闻和报道中的事实错误。约三分之一的人认为，假新闻的问题在于通过社交媒体对真实新闻进行"误读或夸大"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," ↔ readers' misinterpretation；misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news ↔ readers' misinterpretation）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: A) A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online.
B) A Counteraction Against the Over-tweeting Trend.
C) The Accumulation of Mutual Trust on Social Media.
D) The Platforms for Projection of Personal Interests.
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media ↔ A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online；beef up their media literacy skills ↔ A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online）。其余三项中，B 项属以偏概全、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump's use of Twitter. The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform.
paragraphs.zh: Harvard大学的一项新调查发现,超过三分之二的美国年轻人不赞成特朗普总统使用Twitter。这意味着千禧一代更希望来自白宫的新闻经过其他渠道过滤,而不是通过总统的社交媒体平台。

paragraphs.en: Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数美国人依靠社交媒体查看每日新闻标题。然而,随着对所有媒体的不信任加剧,人们可能开始提高他们的媒体素养技能。这种趋势亟需出现。根据Oxford大学的数据,在2016年总统竞选期间,在政治上至关重要的Michigan州,Twitter用户分享的网络内容中近四分之一是假新闻。而为BuzzFeed News进行的一项调查发现,44%的Facebook用户很少或从不信任来自这家媒体巨头的新闻。

paragraphs.en: Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace. A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use "distributed trust" to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias. "Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints," the survey concluded.
paragraphs.zh: 作为数字原住民的年轻人确实在网络空间中越来越善于区分事实与虚构。Knight Foundation对14至24岁年轻人进行的焦点小组调查发现,他们使用"分布式信任"来核实报道。他们交叉核对信息源,并偏好来自不同视角的新闻——尤其是那些公开表明任何偏见的新闻。该调查总结道:"许多年轻人承担了大量个人责任来教育自己,并积极寻求对立的观点。"

paragraphs.en: Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people's reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.
paragraphs.zh: 这种主动研究可能产生另一种效果。University of Wisconsin-Madison在澳大利亚、英国和美国进行的一项2014年调查发现,年轻人对社交媒体的依赖导致了更高的政治参与度。

paragraphs.en: Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in "misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news" via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue. "This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem," says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.
paragraphs.zh: 社交媒体让用户能够更亲密、更即时地体验新闻事件,同时也允许他们将新闻作为其价值观和兴趣的投射进行再次分享。这迫使用户更加意识到自己在传递信息中的角色。Barna研究小组的一项调查发现,美国人对假新闻现象给出的首要原因是"读者错误",而不是编造的故事或报道中的事实错误。大约三分之一的人表示假新闻问题在于通过社交媒体对"实际新闻的误读或夸大"。换句话说,在社交媒体上分享新闻的选择可能是问题的核心。Barna Group主编Roxanne Stone说:"这表明在应对这一问题上存在真正的个人责任。"

paragraphs.en: So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.
paragraphs.zh: 因此,当年轻人批评一位过度发推特的总统时,他们展现出思维技能上的心智自律——以及在何时于社交媒体上分享内容的选择上的自律。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy. DeepMind has almost apologized. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value. The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more. The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.

questions.stem: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?
options: A) It caused conflicts among tech giants.
B) It failed to pay due attention to patients' rights.
C) It fell short of the latter's expectations.
D) It put both sides into a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 B）It failed to pay due attention to patients' rights. 定位句在第 1 段：正是在这一背景下，信息专员 Elizabeth Denham 对 NHS 旗下的 Royal Free 医院信托基金做出了严厉的裁决——该信托在 2015 年依据一份措辞含糊的协议，把 160 万患者的记录交给了 DeepMind，而这份协议远远没有充分顾及患者的权利及其对隐私的期待。正确项与原文构成同义替换（took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy ↔ failed to pay due attention to patients' rights）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The NHS trust responded to Denham's verdict with____
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是细节题，正确答案 C）necessary adjustments. 定位句在第 2 段：DeepMind 已经近乎道歉，NHS 信托基金则已经改正了自己的做法。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The NHS trust has mended its ways ↔ necessary adjustments）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author argues in Paragraph 2 that____
options: A) privacy protection must be secured at all costs.
B) leaking patients' data is worse than selling it.
C) making profits from patients' data is illegal.
D) the value of data comes from the processing of it.
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是主旨题，正确答案 D）the value of data comes from the processing of it. 定位句在第 2 段：但这种区分忽略了一个要点：让数据产生价值的是处理与聚合，而不是仅仅占有这些数据。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value ↔ the value of data comes from the processing of it）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、C 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is____
options: A) the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.
B) the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.
C) the uncontrolled use of new software.
D) the monopoly of big data by tech giants.
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 D）the monopoly of big data by tech giants. 定位句在第 4 段：这种做法（仅用隐私法约束）并没有应对真正的担忧。仅仅说 DeepMind 开发的算法将造福患者、挽救生命还不够；真正要紧的是，这些算法将归属于一家用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources ↔ the monopoly of big data by tech giants）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the application of AI to healthcare is____
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是态度题，正确答案 B）cautious. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. ↔ cautious.；small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. ↔ cautious.）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.
paragraphs.zh: 任何对英国国家医疗服务体系(NHS)与DeepMind之间交易所带来危险的公正评估,都必须首先承认双方的出发点是好的。DeepMind是世界领先的人工智能(AI)公司之一。这项工作应用于医疗保健的潜力非常巨大,但它也可能导致权力进一步集中在科技巨头手中。正是在这样的背景下,信息专员Elizabeth Denham对NHS下属的Royal Free医院信托发出了严厉的裁决,该信托在2015年基于一项含糊的协议将160万患者的记录移交给了DeepMind,而该协议对患者的权利和他们对隐私的期望考虑得太少。

paragraphs.en: DeepMind has almost apologized. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.
paragraphs.zh: DeepMind几乎已经道歉。NHS信托已经改正了做法。未来NHS与DeepMind之间的安排——可能会有很多——将受到仔细审查,以确保已向患者征求所有必要的许可,并且所有不必要的数据已被清除。关于患者知情同意方面有一些教训需要汲取。但隐私并不是本案中唯一的角度,甚至不是最重要的角度。Denham女士选择将责任集中在NHS信托身上,因为根据现行法律,它"控制"着数据,而DeepMind仅仅是"处理"数据。但这种区分忽略了一个要点,即赋予数据价值的是处理和汇总,而不是仅仅拥有数据片段。

paragraphs.en: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
paragraphs.zh: 重大问题是谁应该从我们生活现在产生的所有数据的分析中受益。隐私法建立在可识别的个人信息对个人造成损害这一概念之上。这忽视了监控经济的运作方式。个人数据只有在与无数百万人的数据进行比较时才能获得其价值。

paragraphs.en: The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.
paragraphs.zh: 在这个案例中使用隐私法来遏制科技巨头感觉有些不太适应。这种做法并未解决真正的担忧。仅仅说DeepMind开发的算法将使患者受益并挽救生命是不够的。重要的是,这些算法将属于一家使用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。如果软件承诺能够像现在的药物一样大规模挽救生命,那么可以预期大数据会像大型制药公司那样行事。我们仍处于这场革命的开端,现在的小选择以后可能会产生巨大的后果。要避免数字封建主义的未来,需要进行长期的斗争。Denham女士的报告是一个值得欢迎的开端。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself at the brink of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality. And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS's ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization. Now comes word that everyone involved – Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system's heaviest users – has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions. If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There's no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency's costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS. It is not, however, a sign that they're getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21st century.

questions.stem: The financial problem with the USPS is caused partly by____
options: C) the cost for technical upgrading.
D) the withdrawal of bank support.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 B）its rigid management. 定位句在第 1 段：从根本上说，USPS 正陷于一场历史性的双重挤压：一面是技术变革永久压低了其核心业务——一类邮件——的需求，一面是监管体制不让管理层有足够灵活性去根据新现实调整运营。正确项与原文构成同义替换（a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations ↔ its rigid management）。其余三项中，A 项属把“表现/结果”伪装成“原因”、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the USPS fails to modernize itself due to____
options: A) the interference from interest groups.
B) the inadequate funding from Congress.
C) the shrinking demand for postal service.
D) the incompetence of postal unions.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 A）the interference from interest groups. 定位句在第 2 段：从邮政工会到贺卡商，各种利益集团向 USPS 的最终监管者——国会——施加利己的压力，坚持要求无论邮政服务发生什么变化，他们所依赖的现状的某些方面都要被保护。这就是近年来改革立法屡次失败、USPS 只能靠推迟关键的现代化来勉强支付账单的原因。正确项与原文构成同义替换（interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure ↔ the interference from interest groups）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属答非所问、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions can be addressed by____
options: A) removing its burden of retiree health care.
B) making more investment in new vehicles.
C) adopting a new rate-increase mechanism.
D) attracting more first-class mail users.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 A）removing its burden of retiree health care. 定位句在第 3 段：这笔钱大部分来自每封信永久涨价一便士，以及把邮政退休员工转入 Medicare。后一项措施将在很大程度上抵消每年预提退休人员医保的财务负担，从而解决 USPS 及其工会长期以来的抱怨。正确项与原文构成同义替换（offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care ↔ removing its burden of retiree health care）。其余三项中，B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself at the brink of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.
paragraphs.zh: 美国邮政服务(USPS)继续出现严重亏损。它报告2016财年净亏损56亿美元,这是其支出连续第10年超过收入。与此同时,它有超过1200亿美元的无资金准备负债,主要用于员工医疗和退休费用。这个曾经稳定的联邦机构发现自己处于破产边缘有很多原因。从根本上说,USPS正处于一个历史性的困境之中:技术变革永久性地降低了对其核心产品——一类邮件的需求,而监管结构又使管理层无法灵活调整其业务以适应新现实。

paragraphs.en: And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS's ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.
paragraphs.zh: 从邮政工会到贺卡制造商等各种利益集团对USPS的最终监管者——国会——施加自利性压力,坚持无论邮政服务发生什么变化,他们所依赖的现状都要得到保护。这就是为什么近年来反复的改革立法尝试都失败了,使邮政服务除了推迟至关重要的现代化改造外无法支付账单。

paragraphs.en: Now comes word that everyone involved – Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system's heaviest users – has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions.
paragraphs.zh: 现在传来消息称,所有相关方——民主党人、共和党人、邮政服务、工会和该系统的最大用户——终于就修复系统的计划达成了一致。正在众议院推进的立法将在五年内为USPS节省估计286亿美元,这可以帮助支付新车辆等生存措施的费用。大部分资金将来自每封信一美分的永久性费率增长,以及将邮政退休人员转入Medicare。后一步骤将在很大程度上抵消每年预先拨付退休人员医疗保健的财政负担,从而解决USPS及其工会长期以来的抱怨。

paragraphs.en: If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There's no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency's costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS. It is not, however, a sign that they're getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21st century.
paragraphs.zh: 如果该措施在众议院获得通过,它仍然必须通过参议院——在那里必然会有人指出,这只相当于维持邮政服务运转所需的最低限度,而不是全面改革。USPS的集体谈判没有任何改变,考虑到人事成本占该机构成本的80%,这是一个重大遗漏。同样缺失的是关于取消星期六信件投递的任何讨论。这一常识性改变得到了公众的广泛支持,并将每年为USPS节省20亿美元。但邮政特殊利益集团似乎已经扼杀了它,至少在众议院是这样。围绕该法案出现的共识表明,立法者开始担心USPS会在短期内出现政治上令人尴尬的崩溃。然而,这并不表明他们正在认真考虑为21世纪改造邮政系统。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future. Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering. He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical. When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain? As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything. Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffitied desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum. They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle. But he's also found a kind of insidious prejudice. Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority. Schools in the family of vocational education "have that stereotype…that it's for kids who can't make it academically," he says. On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so. But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all – and the subtle devaluing of anything less – misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained. In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face. There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them. Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap. Koziatek's school is a wake-up call. When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.

paragraphs.en: On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面,这种观点是美国演变的逻辑产物。制造业不再是曾经的经济引擎。美国经济曾经为高中毕业生提供的工作保障已在很大程度上消失了。接受更多教育成为新的原则。我们为孩子们想要更多,这理所应当。

paragraphs.en: But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all – and the subtle devaluing of anything less – misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained.
paragraphs.zh: 但不顾一切地推动所有人获得学士学位——以及对任何更低学历的微妙贬低——忽略了重要的一点:这并非美国经济需要的唯一东西。是的,学士学位能打开更多大门。但即使现在,全国54%的工作是中等技能工作,如建筑业和高技能制造业。但只有44%的工人接受了充分培训。

paragraphs.en: In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face. There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them. Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap.
paragraphs.zh: 换句话说,在工人阶级已让这个国家在政治上发生剧变的时刻,他们对曾经定义美国的机会正在消失感到沮丧,一个显而易见的解决方案正摆在我们面前。工人阶级岗位存在缺口,但最需要这些工作的工人却不具备胜任能力。Koziatek的Manchester School of Technology High School正试图填补这一缺口。

paragraphs.en: Koziatek's school is a wake-up call. When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.
paragraphs.zh: Koziatek的学校是一记警钟。当教育变成一刀切时,它就有可能忽视一个国家天赋的多样性。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: While fossil fuels – coal, oil, gas – still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply, it's clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar. The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line. Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources. But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar. The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years. In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source. In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes. While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift. In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration. President Trump has underlined fossil fuels – especially coal – as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers. The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely. The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles. Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years. While there's a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking. The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up – perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change. What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.

questions.stem: The word "plummeting" (Line 3, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to____.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是词义句意题，正确答案 C）falling 定位句在第 2 段：但越来越多的故事是关于可再生能源（尤其是风能与太阳能）价格的暴跌：过去八年里太阳能板成本下降了 80%，风电机组成本下降了近三分之一。正确项与原文构成同义替换（dropped by 80 percent ↔ falling）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, the use of renewable energy in America____.
options: B) is as extensive as in Europe
D) has proved to be impractical
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 A）is progressing notably 定位句在第 3 段：在世界其他地方（尤其是中国和欧洲）领先的同时，美国也在经历一场显著变革：据美国能源信息署报道，今年 3 月，风能和太阳能首次占到美国发电总量的 10% 以上。正确项与原文构成同义替换（seeing a remarkable shift ↔ is progressing notably；for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent ↔ is progressing notably）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned that in Iowa, ____.
options: A) wind is a widely used energy source
B) wind energy has replaced fossil fuels
C) tech giants are investing in clean energy
D) there is a shortage of clean energy supply
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 A）wind is a widely used energy source 定位句在第 4 段：但这一说法在爱荷华州并不受欢迎——那里风电机组遍布田野，提供该州 36% 的发电量；微软这样的科技巨头也因清洁能源充足而被吸引来建数据中心。正确项与原文构成同义替换（wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation ↔ wind is a widely used energy source）。其余三项中，B 项属过度推断、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about clean energy according to Paragraphs 5&6?
options: A) Its application has boosted battery storage.
B) It is commonly used in car manufacturing.
C) Its continuous supply is becoming a reality.
D) Its sustainable exploitation will remain difficult.
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 C）Its continuous supply is becoming a reality. 定位句在第 5 段："风停日落时怎么办？" 这个问题一直是质疑者快速否定可再生能源的口实；但电池储能能力的提升正在让可再生能源昼夜不间断供电的能力更趋可行。正确项与原文构成同义替换（keep power flowing around the clock more likely ↔ Its continuous supply is becoming a reality；this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years ↔ Its continuous supply is becoming a reality）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that renewable energy____.
options: A) will bring the US closer to other countries
B) will accelerate global environmental change
C) is not really encouraged by the US government
D) is not competitive enough with regard to its cost
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是推断题，正确答案 C）is not really encouraged by the US government 定位句在第 7 段：在全球思想转变的当下，华盛顿（美国政府）做什么或不做什么来推动替代能源，可能越来越无关紧要。正确项与原文构成同义替换（What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy ↔ is not really encouraged by the US government；President Trump has underlined fossil fuels – especially coal – as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. ↔ is not really encouraged by the US government）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: While fossil fuels – coal, oil, gas – still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply, it's clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar. The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管化石燃料——煤炭、石油、天然气——仍然产生世界能源供应的大约85%,但可再生能源如风能和太阳能属于未来这一点比以往任何时候都更加清晰。全球向可再生能源转变的势头正在加快:它们现在占新上线电力来源的一半以上。

paragraphs.en: Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources. But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar. The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years.
paragraphs.zh: 部分增长源于政府和有远见的企业对清洁能源的资助承诺。但这个故事越来越多地与可再生能源价格的暴跌有关,尤其是风能和太阳能。在过去八年中,太阳能电池板的成本下降了80%,风力涡轮机的成本下降了近三分之一。

paragraphs.en: In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source. In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes. While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift. In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration.
paragraphs.zh: 在世界许多地区,可再生能源已经是主要能源来源。例如在苏格兰,风力涡轮机提供的电力足以为95%的家庭供电。在世界其他地区引领潮流的同时,尤其是中国和欧洲,美国也正在经历显著的转变。据美国能源信息署报道,今年3月,风能和太阳能首次占美国发电量的10%以上。

paragraphs.en: President Trump has underlined fossil fuels – especially coal – as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers.
paragraphs.zh: Trump总统强调化石燃料——尤其是煤炭——是经济增长的途径。在最近于Iowa的一次演讲中,他将风能斥为不可靠的能源来源。但这一信息在Iowa并未得到许多人的认同,在那里风力涡轮机遍布田野,提供该州36%的发电量——并且Microsoft等科技巨头正被清洁能源为其数据中心供电的可能性所吸引。

paragraphs.en: The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely.
paragraphs.zh: "当风不吹或太阳不照耀时会发生什么?"这个问题为怀疑者提供了快速反驳。但电池储能容量的提升使其全天候保持电力流动的能力更有可能实现。

paragraphs.en: The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles. Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years.
paragraphs.zh: 这一进步部分是由汽车制造商推动的,他们在电池驱动的电动汽车上下了大赌注。尽管电动汽车目前在道路上仍然罕见,但这一巨额投资可能在未来几年迅速改变这一局面。

paragraphs.en: While there's a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking. The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up – perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change. What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管还有很长的路要走,但可再生能源的趋势线正在飙升。能源来源的变化速度似乎正在加快——也许正好及时产生减缓气候变化的有意义影响。在全球思想转变之际,华盛顿在促进替代能源方面做什么或不做什么可能变得越来越无关紧要。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy are astonishing—Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for ＄13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn't have any physical product at all. What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives. Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through. Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be. What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting? It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what. Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power. But it is clumsy. For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy. By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power. But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too. Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. That would be the people who buy advertising from them – and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies. The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes. It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Facebook acquired WhatsApp for its____.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 B）user information 定位句在第 1 段：WhatsApp 给 Facebook 提供的，是一张关于其用户友谊与社交生活的复杂、细密的关系网。正确项与原文构成同义替换（an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives ↔ user information）。其余三项中，A 项属对照原文直接否定的选项、C 项属张冠李戴：把别家公司的特征安给本题对象、D 项属无中生有：选项内容原文未涉及，均可排除。

questions.stem: Linking phone numbers to Facebook identities may____.
options: C) pose a risk to Facebook users
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是推断题，正确答案 C）pose a risk to Facebook users 定位句在第 2 段：即使不知道消息内容，仅凭谁发给谁这一信息本身就已极具揭示性，至今仍然如此。哪个政治记者、哪个政党党鞭不想知道特蕾莎·梅的政敌当下密谋所在的 WhatsApp 群的成员构成呢？正确项与原文构成同义替换（the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be ↔ pose a risk to Facebook users；Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting ↔ pose a risk to Facebook users）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断：把举例上升为结论、B 项属张冠李戴：用别处的对象冒充本题对象、D 项属答非所问：用前提冒充后果，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to the author, competition law____.
options: A) should serve the new market powers
B) may worsen the economic imbalance
C) should not provide just one legal solution
D) cannot keep pace with the changing market
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 D）cannot keep pace with the changing market 定位句在第 3 段：首先，与数字经济内部的变化节奏相比，它非常缓慢。等到问题被处理和补救时，问题可能已经在市场上消失，并被新的权力滥用所取代。正确项与原文构成同义替换（very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy ↔ cannot keep pace with the changing market；By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace ↔ cannot keep pace with the changing market）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反：把作者立场反转、B 项属无中生有：嫁接未提及的负面后果、C 项属与原文相反：把 only 反转为 not just one，均可排除。

questions.stem: Competition law as presently interpreted can hardly protect Facebook users because____.
options: A) they are not defined as customers
B) they are not financially reliable
C) the services are generally digital
D) the services are paid for by advertisers
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 A）they are not defined as customers 定位句在第 3 段：按现行解释，竞争法处理的是消费者的经济损失，而当这些服务的用户不付费时，这种损失并不明显。这些服务的用户并不是它们的客户。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The users of their services are not their customers ↔ they are not defined as customers；Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them ↔ they are not defined as customers）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念：把 financial 的方向反转、C 项属答非所问：拿话题标签代替真正原因、D 项属答非所问：把附带信息当主因，均可排除。

questions.stem: The ants analogy is used to illustrate____.
options: A) a win-win business model between digital giants
B) a typical competition pattern among digital giants
C) the benefits provided for digital giants' customers
D) the relationship between digital giants and their users
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是例证目的题，正确答案 D）the relationship between digital giants and their users 定位句在第 4 段：他们卖的产品是数据，而我们这些用户把自己的生活转化为数据，为数字巨头服务。正如有些蚂蚁饲养名为蚜虫的小虫，以获取它们进食时产生的蜜露一样，Google 也在饲养我们，以获取我们数字生活产出的数据。正确项与原文构成同义替换（so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield ↔ the relationship between digital giants and their users；Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed ↔ the relationship between digital giants and their users）。其余三项中，A 项属正话反说 + 范围偷换、B 项属张冠李戴：换比喻对象、C 项属以偏概全 + 偷换概念，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy are astonishing—Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for ＄13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn't have any physical product at all. What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives.
paragraphs.zh: 数字经济巨头的力量和野心令人震惊——Amazon刚刚宣布以135亿美元收购高端食品连锁店Whole Foods，但两年前Facebook为收购WhatsApp消息服务支付了更高的价格，而WhatsApp根本没有任何实体产品。WhatsApp提供给Facebook的是其用户友谊和社交生活的复杂而精细的网络。

paragraphs.en: Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through. Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be. What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting? It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what.
paragraphs.zh: Facebook当时向欧盟委员会承诺不会将电话号码与Facebook身份关联，但交易完成后几乎立即违背了这一承诺。即使不知道消息内容是什么，了解谁发送了消息以及发给了谁也极具揭示性，而且现在仍然如此。哪个政治记者、哪个党鞭不想知道Theresa May的敌人目前正在密谋的WhatsApp群组的构成？Whole Foods对Amazon的价值可能不在于它拥有的460家店铺，而在于哪些顾客购买了什么的记录。

paragraphs.en: Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power. But it is clumsy. For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy. By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power. But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too. Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. That would be the people who buy advertising from them – and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies.
paragraphs.zh: 竞争法似乎是解决这些权力失衡的唯一途径。但它很笨拙。首先，与数字经济内部的变化速度相比，它非常缓慢。当一个问题得到解决和补救时，它可能已经在市场上消失，被新的权力滥用所取代。但还有一个更深层次的概念问题。目前解释的竞争法处理的是消费者的财务劣势，而当这些服务的用户不为它们付费时，这一点并不明显。这些服务的用户不是他们的客户。客户应该是那些向他们购买广告的人——而Facebook和Google这两个虚拟巨头主导着数字广告，使所有其他媒体和娱乐公司处于劣势。

paragraphs.en: The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes. It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.
paragraphs.zh: 他们销售的产品是数据，而我们这些用户为了数字巨头的利益将我们的生活转化为数据。正如一些蚂蚁饲养蚜虫以获取它们进食时产生的蜜露，Google也饲养我们以获取我们数字生活产生的数据。蚂蚁让捕食性昆虫远离蚜虫觅食的地方；Gmail让垃圾邮件发送者远离我们的收件箱。即使双方都受益，这感觉也不像是一种人性化或民主的关系。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" – the ability to focus without distraction. There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work – be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day. Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it. Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time. "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month. Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes. Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day – in particular how we craft our to-do lists. Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day. While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results. In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy". "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues. Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate. When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient. "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.

questions.stem: The key to mastering the art of deep work is to____.
options: A) keep to your focus time
D) seize every minute to work
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 A）keep to your focus time 定位句在第 2 段：无论采用哪种方法,关键都是确定你专注时间的长度,并坚持下去。正确项与原文构成同义替换（determine your length of focus time and stick to it ↔ keep to your focus time）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属张冠李戴、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The study in the early 1980s cited by Harford shows that____.
options: A) distractions may actually increase efficiency
B) daily schedules are indispensable to studying
C) students are hardly motivated by monthly goals
D) detailed plans may not be as fruitful as expected
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 D）detailed plans may not be as fruitful as expected 定位句在第 5 段：尽管研究者们原以为结构良好的日计划在执行任务时最有效,但他们错了:详尽的日计划反倒让学生失去了动力。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students ↔ detailed plans may not be as fruitful as expected；detailed daily plans ↔ detailed plans）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Newport, idleness is____.
options: A) a desirable mental state for busy people
B) a major contributor to physical health
C) an effective way to save time and energy
D) an essential factor in accomplishing any work
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 D）an essential factor in accomplishing any work 定位句在第 7 段：闲适并不仅仅是度假、放纵或恶习;它对大脑就如同维生素 D 对身体一样不可或缺……反讽的是,正是闲适才使得任何工作得以完成。正确项与原文构成同义替换（necessary to getting any work done ↔ an essential factor in accomplishing any work）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Pillay believes that our brains' shift between being focused and unfocused____.
options: A) can result in psychological well-being
B) can bring about greater efficiency
C) is aimed at better balance in work
D) is driven by task urgency
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 B）can bring about greater efficiency 定位句在第 8 段：当我们的大脑在专注于某项任务与放空之间来回切换时,它们往往更高效。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they tend to be more efficient ↔ can bring about greater efficiency）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属过度推断、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: This text is mainly about____.
options: A) ways to relieve the tension of busy life
B) approaches to getting more done in less time
C) the key to eliminating distractions
D) the cause of the lack of focus time
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是主旨题，正确答案 B）approaches to getting more done in less time 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Another approach to getting more done in less time ↔ approaches to getting more done in less time；get more done in less time ↔ getting more done in less time）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" – the ability to focus without distraction.
paragraphs.zh: 为了对抗将忙碌视为优点的陷阱,《深度工作:在分心世界中专注成功的法则》一书的作者Cal Newport建议培养"深度工作"的习惯——即不受干扰地专注的能力。

paragraphs.en: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work – be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day. Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
paragraphs.zh: 掌握深度工作艺术有多种方法——无论是专门用于特定任务的长时间静修、养成日常习惯,还是采取"新闻工作者式"的方法在一天中抓住深度工作的时刻。无论采用哪种方法,关键是确定你的专注时长并坚持下去。

paragraphs.en: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time. "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month. Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.
paragraphs.zh: Newport还建议采用"深度日程安排"来对抗持续的干扰,在更短的时间内完成更多工作。他写道:"在任何给定时刻,我都应该为未来大约一个月安排好深度工作。一旦列入日程,我就会像对待医生预约或重要会议一样保护这段时间。"

paragraphs.en: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day – in particular how we craft our to-do lists. Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.
paragraphs.zh: 在更短时间内完成更多工作的另一种方法是重新思考如何安排一天的优先事项——特别是我们如何制定待办事项清单。《混乱:无序的力量如何改变我们的生活》一书的作者Tim Harford指出了20世纪80年代初的一项研究,该研究将本科生分为两组:一些人被建议制定月度目标和学习活动;另一些人被要求更详细地规划活动和目标,逐日进行。

paragraphs.en: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然研究人员认为结构良好的每日计划在执行任务时最有效,但他们错了:详细的每日计划削弱了学生的积极性。Harford认为,不可避免的干扰常常使每日待办事项清单失效,而在这样的清单中为即兴发挥留出空间可以获得最佳结果。

paragraphs.en: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".
paragraphs.zh: 为了充分利用我们的专注力和精力,我们还需要拥抱休息时间,或者如Newport所建议的,"变得懒惰"。

paragraphs.en: "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.
paragraphs.zh: 他认为:"闲散不仅仅是假期、放纵或恶习;它对大脑来说就像维生素D对身体一样不可或缺……[闲散]自相矛盾地是完成任何工作所必需的。"

paragraphs.en: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate. When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
paragraphs.zh: 哈佛医学院精神病学助理教授Srini Pillay认为,休息时间与生产力之间这种违反直觉的联系可能源于我们大脑的运作方式。当我们的大脑在专注和不专注于某项任务之间切换时,它们往往会更有效率。

paragraphs.en: "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.
paragraphs.zh: Pillay说:"人们没有意识到的是,为了完成这些任务,他们需要同时使用大脑中的专注和非专注回路。"

[7] left alone in the room, the students who did not know which ones would shock them clicked more pens and incurred more shocks than the students who knew what would [8] . blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 B）resolve。resolve 此处取"解决、消除"义，resolve uncertainty 正是"消除不确定"，与下句的 need to know、satisfy their curiosity 同义复述对得上。。其余三项：A）protect 对象反了、C）discuss 程度太轻、D）ignore 正话反说，均可排除。
第 2 空正确答案 D）seek。seek 即"寻求、设法"，seek to satisfy their curiosity = 想方设法满足好奇心，与 inherent need 的强度、与下文学生主动按电击笔的行为一致。。其余三项：A）refuse 方向反、B）wait 动作太被动、C）regret 时间错位，均可排除。
第 3 空正确答案 A）hurt。hurt"伤害、让人难受"与首句 painful 同义复述，the answer will hurt = 答案会让人难受，正是本段论点。。其余三项：B）last 维度错、C）mislead 义不沾边、D）rise 搭配怪，均可排除。
第 4 空正确答案 D）expose。expose sb to sth 即"使某人接触/暴露于……"，expose themselves to unpleasant stimuli 是心理学实验里描述"自愿置身于不快刺激"的标准说法。。其余三项：A）alert 搭配错向、B）tie 义不贴、C）treat 框架错，均可排除。
第 5 空正确答案 C）trial。trial 在实验语境下即"试验、回合"，For one trial = 在其中一次试验里，正好引出下文电击笔的具体场景，与上句 four experiments 形成总—分关系。。其余三项：A）message 话题错、B）review 义偏、D）concept 维度错，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 D）deliver。deliver 在科技/医学语境里常表"释放、施加"，deliver an electric shock = 释放一次电击，是英语里描述"装置施加电击"的固定说法。。其余三项：A）remove 反向、B）weaken 搭配怪、C）interrupt 对象错，均可排除。

第 9 空正确答案 C）such as。such as"诸如"专门用于在上位词后面引出具体例子，正好对应 other stimuli + 两个具体实例的总—分结构。。其余三项：A）rather than 对比错、B）regardless of 义不沾、D）owing to 因果不存在，均可排除。
第 10 空正确答案 A）discover。discover"发现、探索"与 Curiosity 对应——the drive to discover 即"探索的冲动"，与下句把它视为科学进步的源泉自然衔接。。其余三项：B）forgive 话题错、C）forget 方向反、D）disagree 话题错，均可排除。
第 11 空正确答案 D）food。food"食物"与 shelter"住所"是人类最基本的生存需求，两者并列正好支撑 basic drives 的定性，与马斯洛底层需求一致。。其余三项：A）pay 层级偏、B）marriage 层级偏、C）schooling 层级偏，均可排除。
第 12 空正确答案 A）lead to。lead to"导致、带来"——curiosity can lead to new scientific advances = 好奇心能带来新的科学进展，正好是 good instinct 的正面证据。。其余三项：B）rest on 方向反、C）learn from 对象错、D）begin with 义偏，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 C）inquiry。inquiry"探询、探究"与 curiosity 同义，such inquiry = 这种探究，回指上句的好奇心，并与下文 backfire 形成反差。。其余三项：A）withdrawal 义反、B）persistence 回指对象错、D）diligence 回指对象错，均可排除。

第 16 空正确答案 B）predict。predict"预测、预想"与 imagining ahead of time 同义，predict how they would feel = 预想自己会有什么感受。。其余三项：A）overlook 方向反、C）design 话题错、D）conceal 义反，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 C）choose。choose"选择"——less likely to choose to see = 更不愿意选择去看，正好刻画"对策起效"的行为减少。。其余三项：A）remember 话题错、B）promise 色彩错、D）pretend 义偏，均可排除。

第 18 空正确答案 D）outcome。outcome"结果"——imagining the outcome of following through on one's curiosity ahead of time = 事先想象顺着好奇心做下去的结果，与段尾 long-term consequences 完美同义。。其余三项：A）relief 色彩偏、B）plan 时序错、C）duty 话题错，均可排除。

Because humans have an inherent need to [1] uncertainty, according to a recent study in Psychological Science. The new research reveals that the need to know is so strong that people will [2] to satisfy their curiosity even when it is clear the answer will [3] .
paragraphs.zh: 为什么人们会阅读负面的网络评论并做其他明显会带来痛苦的事情?根据《心理科学》杂志最近的一项研究,这是因为人类有一种内在的需求去消解不确定性。这项新研究揭示,求知的需求是如此强烈,以至于即使明确知道答案会造成伤害,人们仍会寻求满足他们的好奇心。

paragraphs.zh: 在一系列四项实验中,芝加哥大学和威斯康星商学院的行为科学家测试了学生为满足好奇心而使自己暴露于不愉快刺激的意愿。在其中一项试验中,每位参与者被展示一堆钢笔,研究人员声称这些钢笔来自之前的一个实验。其中的转折是什么?有一半的钢笔在按下时会产生电击。

In a final experiment, participants who were encouraged to [16] how they would feel after viewing an unpleasant picture were less likely to [17] to see such an image.
