"We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation," Ferraro says.
paragraphs.zh: Ferraro分析了卫星数据,显示了2008年至2012年期间的年度森林损失——包括印度尼西亚扶贫计划逐步实施期间——涵盖15个省的7468个森林村庄。Ferraro说:"我们看到该计划与森林砍伐减少30%相关。"

paragraphs.en: That's likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says. Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests.
paragraphs.zh: Ferraro说,这可能是因为农村贫困人口正在将这笔钱用作应对恶劣天气的临时保险政策。通常情况下,如果降雨推迟,人们可能会清理土地种植更多水稻来补充收成。

paragraphs.en: Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody's guess. Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access. And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what's good for people may also be good for the environment. Even if this program didn't reduce poverty, Ferraro says, "the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs."
paragraphs.zh: 这项研究是否适用于其他地方,谁也说不准。Ferraro认为,由于种植水稻的重要性和市场准入等共性,研究结果可能适用于亚洲其他地区。无论可迁移性如何,该研究表明,对人有益的事情也可能对环境有益。Ferraro说,即使该计划没有减少贫困,"仅就二氧化碳排放而言,避免森林砍伐的价值就超过了该计划的成本。"

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?). I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter. Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance. How do we explain this trend? During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs. The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm. But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous. Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile. One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. "Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed). A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, the author's posts on Twitter ____
options: A) changed people's impression of the Victorians.
B) highlighted social media's role in Victorian studies.
C) re-evaluated the Victorian's notion of public image.
D) illustrated the development of Victorian photography.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 A）changed people's impression of the Victorians. 定位句在第 1 段：人们惊讶地看到证据，原来维多利亚人也会享受、会笑、确实笑过。他们注意到，维多利亚人突然变得更像 "人" 了——相隔我们一百多年的时空，在共同的笑声体验中消融。正确项与原文构成同义替换（People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun ↔ changed people's impression of the Victorians；the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human ↔ changed people's impression of the Victorians）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author say about the Victorian portraits he has collected?
options: A) They are in popular use among historians.
B) They are rare among photographs of that age.

questions.stem: Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was____

"nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever" ↔ a deep-root belief；it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons ↔ a deep-root belief）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following questions does the text answer?

B) Why did the Victorians start to view photographs?

I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名总在寻找那些让我们重新评价过去的文字或图像的历史学家，我开始专注于寻找维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片(还有什么比这更能打破19世纪古板拘谨的形象呢?)。我找到了不少这样的照片，而且自从我开始在Twitter上发布它们以来，它们引起了相当大的轰动。人们惊讶地看到证据表明维多利亚时代的人也有乐趣，能够而且确实会笑。他们注意到，随着我们对笑声的共同体验消除了横亘在我们之间的百年左右的时光，维多利亚时代的人突然显得更加人性化了。

paragraphs.en: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance. How do we explain this trend?
paragraphs.zh: 当然，我需要承认，我收藏的"微笑的维多利亚时代人"照片只占1840年至1900年间创作的大量摄影肖像目录中的极小一部分，其中大多数照片显示的是被拍摄者在彩绘背景前痛苦而僵硬地摆姿势，或茫然地凝视着中距离处。我们如何解释这一趋势？

paragraphs.en: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs. The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.
paragraphs.zh: 在19世纪40年代和50年代摄影的早期，曝光时间出了名地长：银版摄影法(在镀银铜板上成像)可能需要几分钟才能完成，导致图像模糊，因为被拍摄者移动了位置或调整了肢体。想到在相机执行其神奇职责时保持固定的笑容实在难以想象，因此不置可否的茫然凝视成为常态。

paragraphs.en: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous. Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.
paragraphs.zh: 但到了19世纪80年代，曝光时间已经快得多了，Box Brownie和其他便携式相机的引入意味着，尽管按今天的数字标准来说仍然缓慢，但曝光几乎是瞬时的。到19世纪90年代，捕捉自然的微笑相对容易了，因此我们必须到别处寻找维多利亚时代的人为何仍然犹豫微笑的解释。

paragraphs.en: One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. "Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).
paragraphs.zh: 一个解释可能是通过俗气的露齿笑所展现出的尊严丧失。"大自然给了我们嘴唇来遮住牙齿，"一句流行的维多利亚时代格言如是说，暗指在正规牙科诞生之前，口腔的卫生状况往往令人震惊。在维多利亚时代社会，一口健康、干净、整齐的"珍珠白"牙齿是罕见的景象，是超级富豪的专属(即便如此，牙齿卫生也不能得到保证)。

paragraphs.en: A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".
paragraphs.zh: 露齿的笑容(尤其是当牙齿有缺口或发黑时)缺乏品味：醉汉、流浪汉和音乐厅表演者可能会像Lewis Carroll笔下露出牙龈的Cheshire Cat那样做鬼脸和咧嘴大笑，但这对于教养良好的人来说不是得体的样子。即使是Mark Twain这样一个喜欢开怀大笑的人也说，在摄影肖像方面，"没有什么比永远定格的愚蠢、傻气的微笑更糟糕的了"。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals'. That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet. Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either. The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV. Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own. On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move. But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism." In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication. The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act. It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.

questions.stem: There has long been concern that broadband providers would____
options: A) bring web-based firms under control.
B) slow down the traffic on their network.
C) show partiality in treating clients.
D) intensify competition with their rivals.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 C）show partiality in treating clients. 定位句在第 1 段：从宽带发展早期起，消费者权益倡导者和互联网公司就担心：销售宽带连接的有线电视和电话公司，有权力也有动机偏袒与自己关联的网站，而冷落对手的网站。正确项与原文构成同义替换（favor affiliated websites over their rivals' ↔ show partiality in treating clients）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属无中生有、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: Faced with the demand for net neutrality rules, the FCC____
options: A) sticks to an out-of-date order.
C) has issued a special resolution.
D) has allowed the states to intervene.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 B）takes an anti-regulatory stance. 定位句在第 2 段：由共和党主笔的这份命令不仅废除了 FCC 在 2015 年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则，还否定了 FCC 自身要求宽带商做任何事的监管权。该命令还宣布州和地方政府也不能监管宽带商。正确项与原文构成同义替换（eliminated the strict net neutrality rules ↔ takes an anti-regulatory stance；rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything ↔ takes an anti-regulatory stance）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can be learned about AT&T from Paragraph 3?
options: A) It protects against unfair competition.
B) It engages in anti-competitive practices.
C) It is under the FCC's investigation.
D) It is in pursuit of quality service.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 B）It engages in anti-competitive practices. 定位句在第 3 段：FCC 辩称，会有别的机构防止反竞争行为，比如像 AT&T 这种宽带集团偏袒自家流媒体服务、损害 Netflix 和 Apple TV 的利益。正确项与原文构成同义替换（anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV ↔ engages in anti-competitive practices）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Judge Patricia Millett argues that the appeals court's decision____
options: C) is at odds with its earlier rulings.
D) is out of touch with reality.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 D）is out of touch with reality. 定位句在第 4 段：但 Millett 法官在协同意见中说得对："这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实"，并表示国会或最高法院可以介入，"以免把互联网监管困在技术时代错置之中"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service ↔ is out of touch with reality）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author argue in the last paragraph?
options: A) Congress needs to take action to ensure net neutrality.
B) The FCC should be put under strict supervision.
C) Rules need to be set to diversify online services.
D) Broadband providers' rights should be protected.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）Congress needs to take action to ensure net neutrality. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（cry out for Congress to act ↔ Congress needs to take action to ensure net neutrality；create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online ↔ to ensure net neutrality）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals'. That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet.
paragraphs.zh: 从宽带发展早期开始,消费者权益倡导者和网络公司就担心,销售宽带连接的有线电视和电话公司有能力也有动机偏袒关联网站而非竞争对手。这就是为什么人们强烈要求制定规则,防止宽带提供商在网上挑选赢家和输家,保护一直是互联网命脉的自由和创新。

paragraphs.en: Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,这一要求几乎不可能实现——部分原因是来自宽带提供商、反监管保守派和法院的阻力。联邦上诉法院周二再次介入,但它非但没有提供急需的解决方案,反而延长了这场斗争。美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院审理的是联邦通信委员会在2017年以党派立场投票通过的关于网络中立的最新立场。这项由共和党撰写的命令不仅废除了联邦通信委员会在2015年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则,还否认了该委员会要求宽带提供商做任何事情的权力。该命令还宣布州和地方政府也不能监管宽带提供商。

paragraphs.en: The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV. Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own.
paragraphs.zh: 该委员会辩称,其他机构将防范反竞争行为,比如像AT&T这样的宽带提供商集团以牺牲Netflix和Apple TV为代价偏袒自己的视频流媒体服务。然而,联邦通信委员会也终止了对那些对竞争对手的流媒体服务设置数据上限而对自己的服务不设上限的宽带提供商的调查。

paragraphs.en: On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move. But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism."
paragraphs.zh: 周二,上诉法院一致维持了2017年放松对宽带提供商监管的命令,援引了最高法院2005年支持类似放松监管举措的裁决。但法官Patricia Millett在协同意见中正确地指出,'这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实',并表示国会或最高法院可以介入以'避免将互联网监管困在技术过时主义中'。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时,法院推翻了联邦通信委员会试图阻止所有州网络中立规则的做法,同时保留了该委员会优先否决破坏其命令的个别州法律的权力。这意味着会有更多像司法部与加利福尼亚州之间正在进行的这类战斗,该州在联邦通信委员会放弃职责后颁布了一项严格的网络中立法。

paragraphs.en: The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act. It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.
paragraphs.zh: 联邦通信委员会无休止的法律战和反复无常迫切需要国会采取行动。国会需要一劳永逸地赋予该委员会明确权力,禁止宽带提供商干预其网络上的流量,并制定明确规则保护网络的开放性和创新。

blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 C）peaks。三段式趋势：先升、再平、后降。其余三项：A）pauses 义不符：暂停不等于到达高点、B）returns 义不符：返回需有先前基准、D）fades 义反：提前下降与后文重复矛盾，均可排除。
第 2 空正确答案 D）generally。as we age 表明是普遍随龄规律。其余三项：A）alternatively 义不符：表「或者、替代地」、B）formally 义不符：表「正式地」、C）accidentally 义反：偶然与「随龄普遍」相悖，均可排除。
第 3 空正确答案 A）while。「不可避免」对「未必如此」的对比。其余三项：B）since 逻辑反：强加因果、C）once 逻辑反：表时间条件「一旦」、D）until 逻辑反：表时间「直到」，均可排除。
第 4 空正确答案 B）accumulation。与 muscle loss 并列、共同导致衰退。其余三项：A）detection 义不符：表「检测、发现」、C）consumption 义反：表「消耗、消减」、D）separation 义不符：表「分离」，均可排除。
第 5 空正确答案 A）possibility。suggests + might 表推测、未定论。其余三项：B）decision 义不符：表「决定」、C）goal 义不符：表「目标」、D）requirement 义反：表「必要条件、要求」过强，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 A）delay。与 prevent 并列、对象是「衰退」。其余三项：B）ensure 逻辑反：确保衰退发生、C）seek 逻辑反：寻求衰退、D）utilize 义不符：表「利用」，均可排除。
第 7 空正确答案 C）included。数据「含有」各项测量值。其余三项：A）modified 义不符：表「修改」、B）supported 义不符：表「支持」、D）predicted 义不符：表「预测」，均可排除。
第 8 空正确答案 B）compared。把脂肪数据「对照」智力变化。其余三项：A）devoted 义不符：devote...to 表「投入于」、C）converted 义不符：表「转换」、D）applied 义不符：apply...to 表「应用于」，均可排除。
第 9 空正确答案 A）with。people ___ higher fat 表「拥有较高脂肪的人」。其余三项：B）above 搭配不当：表「在……之上」、C）by 搭配不当：表方式或幅度、D）against 义反：表「对抗、逆」，均可排除。
第 10 空正确答案 C）scored。score worse on measures 表「测试得分更差」。其余三项：A）lived 搭配不当：live 不接 on measures 表得分、B）managed 搭配不当：manage 不与 on measures 连用、D）played 搭配不当：play 多用于比赛而非测验得分，均可排除。
第 11 空正确答案 D）went by。六年期 → years went by 表「岁月流逝」。其余三项：A）ran out 义不符：表「用完、耗尽」、B）set off 义不符：表「出发、引发」、C）drew in 义不符：多指「天渐黑、临近」，均可排除。
第 12 空正确答案 B）attributable。association 由免疫变化「导致」→ 归因。其余三项：A）superior 义不符：be superior to 表「优于」、C）parallel 义不符：be parallel to 表「与……平行」、D）resistant 义反：be resistant to 表「抵抗」，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 C）involved。与女性「免疫变化起作用」相对照。其余三项：A）restored 义不符：表「恢复」、B）isolated 义不符：表「被孤立、分离」、D）controlled 义不符：表「被控制」，均可排除。
第 14 空正确答案 D）explain。研究的目的是弄清差异、进而指导用药。其余三项：A）alter 义不符：表「改变」、B）spread 义不符：表「传播、扩散」、C）remove 义不符：表「消除」，均可排除。
第 15 空正确答案 D）treatments。全文落点是「如何应对衰退」的对策。其余三项：A）compensations 义不符：表「补偿、赔偿」、B）symptoms 义不符：表「症状」、C）demands 义不符：表「需求、要求」，均可排除。
第 16 空正确答案 B）Meanwhile。机制未明 vs 已有可行步骤，平行推进。其余三项：A）Likewise 逻辑反：表「同样地」需前后同类、C）Therefore 逻辑反：强加因果、D）Instead 逻辑反：表「相反、取而代之」，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 D）take。take steps 表「采取措施」。其余三项：A）change 搭配不当：change steps 非固定表达、B）watch 搭配不当：watch steps 表「留神脚下」、C）count 搭配不当：count steps 表「数步数」，均可排除。
第 18 空正确答案 A）well-being。protect physical and mental ___ → 保护身心健康。其余三项：B）process 义不符：表「过程」、C）formation 义不符：表「形成」、D）coordination 义不符：表「协调」，均可排除。
第 19 空正确答案 A）level。maintain or increase 要求可增减的「量/水平」。其余三项：B）love 义不符：表「热爱」、C）knowledge 义不符：表「知识」、D）space 义不符：表「空间」，均可排除。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind. We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022. That is a very short timeline. The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one. For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. That does not always happen. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy. Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans. When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle. Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high. With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed. In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere. As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel. Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it. But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned. That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.

questions.stem: Research by the World Economic Forum suggests____.
options: A) an increase in full-time employment
B) an urgent demand for new job skills
C) a steady growth of job opportunities
D) a controversy about the "core skills"
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 B）an urgent demand for new job skills 定位句在第 1 段：世界经济论坛的研究发现，到 2022 年，岗位中约 42% 的"核心技能"将发生变化。正确项与原文构成同义替换（42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022 ↔ an urgent demand for new job skills；That is a very short timeline. ↔ urgent）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: AT&T is cited to show____.
options: A) an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy
B) an immediate need for government support
C) the importance of staff appraisal standards
D) the characteristics of reskilling programs
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy 定位句在第 2 段：AT&T 常被誉为典范——这家公司选择大规模再培训计划，而不是采取"先解雇再招新"的策略。正确项与原文构成同义替换（decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy ↔ an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy）。其余三项中，B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada____.
options: A) have driven up labour costs
B) have proved to be inconsistent
C) have met with fierce opposition
D) have appeared to be insufficient
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 D）have appeared to be insufficient 定位句在第 2 段：加拿大及其他地方的努力充其量也只能说是"懒散"，由此造成的局面是：我们常听到雇主求人难，哪怕在失业率本就高的时段和地区也是如此。正确项与原文构成同义替换（languid at best ↔ have appeared to be insufficient；we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high ↔ insufficient）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: We can learn from Paragraph 3 that there was____.
options: A) a call for policy adjustment
B) a change in hiring practices
C) a lack of medical workers
D) a sign of economic recovery
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 C）a lack of medical workers 定位句在第 3 段：举一个明显的例子：在医疗领域，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医护人员仍然明显短缺。正确项与原文构成同义替换（clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel ↔ a lack of medical workers）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Scandinavian Airlines decided to____.
options: A) create job vacancies for the unemployed
B) prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs
C) retrain their cabin staff for better services
D) finance their staff's college education
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是细节题，正确答案 B）prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs 定位句在第 4 段：在被迫让 90% 的乘务员停工时，北欧航空决定启动一个短期再培训项目，把被解雇的员工再培训以支援医院员工。正确项与原文构成同义替换（reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff ↔ prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind. We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022. That is a very short timeline.
paragraphs.zh: "再培训"听起来像是一个流行词，但如果我们计划拥有一个不让大量潜在劳动者掉队的未来，它实际上是一项必需。我们知道我们正在进入一个需求岗位将快速变化的时期，现有岗位的要求也会随之变化。世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，平均42%的岗位角色"核心技能"将发生变化。这是一个非常短的时间线。

paragraphs.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one. For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. That does not always happen. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy. Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans. When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle. Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
paragraphs.zh: 谁应该为再培训买单是一个棘手的问题。对于单个公司而言，诱惑总是解雇技能不再有需求的员工，并用那些拥有所需技能的人取而代之。但情况并非总是如此。AT&T常被视为决定实施大规模再培训计划而非采取解雇再招聘策略的公司的黄金标准。包括亚马逊和迪士尼在内的其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。然而,当技能不匹配出现在更广泛的经济领域时,焦点通常转向政府来处理。加拿大和其他地方的努力可以说充其量是疲软的,并给我们带来了这样一种局面:我们经常听到雇主恳求招工,即使是在失业率很高的时期和地区。

paragraphs.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed. In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere. As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
paragraphs.zh: 随着疫情的到来,失业率确实非常高。2月份,加拿大和美国的失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%,处于几代人以来的最低水平,各地都出现了劳动力短缺。到5月份,这些比率已飙升至13.3%和13.7%,尽管许多劳动力短缺已经消失,但并非所有短缺都消失了。以医疗领域为例,疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医务人员仍然明显短缺。

paragraphs.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it. But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned. That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
paragraphs.zh: 当然,你不可能在几周内把一个失业的服务员培训成医生,无论由谁买单。但即使你无法弥合那种差距,也许你可以弥合其他差距,而这样做将使所有相关方受益。瑞典的情况似乎就是如此:当被迫让90%的机舱乘务员休假时,斯堪的纳维亚航空公司决定启动一个短期再培训项目,对下岗员工进行再培训以支援医院工作人员。这项努力是集体性的,涉及其他公司以及一所瑞典大学。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines. In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit. Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food. The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s. A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health. Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision? According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production. That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs. There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave. To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively—meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production. But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help. There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis. Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields. Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg—which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes—we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production. Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs. That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.

questions.stem: Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would____.
options: A) be hindered by its population growth
B) contribute to the nation's well-being
C) become a priority of the government
D) pose a challenge to its farming industry
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 B）contribute to the nation's well-being 定位句在第 2 段：支持者主张，重回自给自足将提振农业、政治主权、甚至国民健康。正确项与原文构成同义替换（even the nation's health ↔ contribute to the nation's well-being）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有：把背景信息当成论点内容、C 项属无中生有：替政府表态、D 项属与原文相反：动词极性反转，均可排除。

questions.stem: The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK____.
options: A) farmland has been inefficiently utilized
C) most land is used for meat and dairy production
D) more green fields will be converted for farming
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 C）most land is used for meat and dairy production 定位句在第 3 段：据利兹大学一份关于英国食品生产的报告，英国 85% 的国土面积与肉奶生产相关。正确项与原文构成同义替换（85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production ↔ most land is used for meat and dairy production）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断：把事实数字升级成价值评价、B 项属偷换概念：把「需要更多 X」偷换成「X 需要改革」、D 项属与原文相反：极性反转，均可排除。

questions.stem: Crop-growing in the UK is restricted due to____.
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 C）its natural conditions 定位句在第 5 段：英国以畜牧业为主是有原因的：其大部分地形的土壤或气候不适合商业化种植作物。正确项与原文构成同义替换（doesn't have the right soil or climate ↔ its natural conditions）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有：常识性归因、B 项属偷换概念：把段内相关词当成因果原因、D 项属偷换概念：抓住关键词 commercial 改写其语法功能，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that British people____.
options: A) rely largely on imports for fresh produce
B) enjoy a steady rise in fruit consumption
C) are seeking effective ways to cut calorie intake
D) are trying to grow new varieties of grains
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是推断题，正确答案 A）rely largely on imports for fresh produce 定位句在第 6 段：目前英国消费的水果蔬菜仅有 23% 是本土所产，即便采取最极端的措施也只能满足 30% 的新鲜农产品需求。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown ↔ rely largely on imports for fresh produce）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有：杜撰时间趋势、C 项属与原文相反：把「需要更多」反转成「努力削减」、D 项属无中生有：捏造科研行动，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author's attitude to food self-sufficiency in the UK is____.
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是态度题，正确答案 B）doubtful 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision? ↔ doubtful；wouldn't help ↔ doubtful）。其余三项中，A 项属态度词「对象错位」、C 项属态度词色彩误配、D 项属与原文相反：极性反转，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines. In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
paragraphs.zh: 据预测，到2050年全球人口将接近100亿，并且有预测称某些地区的农业生产需要增加近一倍才能跟上步伐,粮食安全正日益成为头条新闻。在英国,最近它也成为一个热门话题,原因相当特殊:英国脱欧。

paragraphs.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food. The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s. A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health. Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision?
paragraphs.zh: 一些人将英国脱欧视为扭转英国近期进口粮食趋势的一个机会。该国仅生产其消费粮食的约60%,而在20世纪80年代末这一比例接近四分之三。有观点认为,回归自给自足将促进农业、政治主权甚至国民健康。听起来很好——但这一愿景的可行性如何?

paragraphs.en: According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production. That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
paragraphs.zh: 根据英国利兹大学一份关于英国粮食生产的报告,该国85%的土地总面积与肉类和乳制品生产相关。这供应了消费量的80%,因此即使将整个国家都覆盖上畜牧农场,我们也无法满足所有肉类和乳制品需求。

paragraphs.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave. To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively—meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
paragraphs.zh: 这些数字有许多附加说明,但它们仍然严峻。要变得更加自给自足,英国需要大幅减少动物性食品的消费,并且可能还需要更集约化地耕作——这意味着更少的绿地和更多的工厂式生产。

paragraphs.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help. There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis. Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields. Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg—which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes—we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
paragraphs.zh: 但转向以植物为主的饮食也无济于事。英国以畜牧业为主有一个很好的理由:其大部分地形没有合适的土壤或气候来进行商业化作物种植。该国只有25%的土地适合种植作物,其中大部分已被耕地占用。即使我们将所有适合的土地都转换为果蔬田——这将涉及占用所有自然保护区并将成千上万的人从家中迁出——我们也只能实现作物产量30%的提升。

paragraphs.en: Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs. That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
paragraphs.zh: 目前英国消费的水果和蔬菜中只有23%是本土种植的,因此即使采取最极端的措施,我们也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。这还是在我们寻找空间种植谷物、糖类、种子和油料作物之前,而这些作物为我们提供了当前卡路里摄入的绝大部分。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley. Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for "productivity" software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world. Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products. Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many "acqui-hires" that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent. To Microsoft's critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path. "They bought the seedlings and closed them down," complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors. Microsoft declined to comment. Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: "I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on. But are they good for the American economy? I don't know." The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question. This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade. Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach. Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point. Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year. However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a "buy and kill" tactic to simply close them down.

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive. In one study of the ability she called "thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness. Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings. Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory. Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing. Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating. Accuracy dropped dramatically. Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression. She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners. Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection. "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing. But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine. Much of our social life is like that." Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences. College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale. And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process. Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances. In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech). Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," "hunches," "my heart"). Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest. Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.

paragraphs.en: Travel on a London bus and you'll [3] see how this works with drivers. Watch people get on and show their tickets. Are they carefully inspected? Never. Do people get on without paying? Of course! Are there inspectors to [4] that people have paid? Possibly, but very few. And people who run for the bus? They are [5] . How about jumping lights? Buses do so almost as frequently as cyclists.
paragraphs.zh: 乘坐伦敦公交车,你很快就会看到这在司机身上是如何体现的。观察人们上车并出示车票。车票会被仔细检查吗?从来不会。有人不付钱就上车吗?当然有!有检票员检查人们是否付费吗?可能有,但非常少。那些追赶公交车的人呢?他们被忽视了。闯红灯呢?公交车闯红灯的频率几乎和骑自行车的人一样高。

paragraphs.en: Why? Because the target is [6] . People complained that buses were late and infrequent. [7] , the number of buses and bus lanes was increased, and drivers were [8] or punished according to the time they took. And drivers hit these targets. But they [9] hit cyclists. If the target was changed to [10] , you would have more inspectors and more sensitive pricing. If the criterion changed to safety, you would get more [11] drivers who obeyed traffic laws. But both these criteria would be at the expense of time.
paragraphs.zh: 为什么?因为目标是准点。人们抱怨公交车晚点且班次不频繁。因此,公交车数量和公交专用道增加了,司机根据他们所花费的时间受到奖励或惩罚。司机们达到了这些目标。但他们也撞到了骑自行车的人。如果目标改为收入,你会有更多检票员和更灵活的定价。如果标准改为安全,你会得到更谨慎、遵守交通法规的司机。但这两个标准都将以时间为代价。

paragraphs.en: There is another [12] : people became immensely inventive in hitting targets. Have you [13] that you can leave on a flight an hour late but still arrive on time? Tailwinds? Of course not! Airlines have simply changed the time a [14] is meant to take. A one-hour flight is now billed as a two-hour flight.
paragraphs.zh: 还有另一个问题:人们在达成目标方面变得极其善于创新。你有没有注意到,你可以晚一个小时起飞但仍能准点到达?顺风?当然不是!航空公司只是改变了行程应该花费的时间。一小时的航班现在被标注为两小时的航班。

paragraphs.en: The [15] of the story is simple. Most jobs are multidimensional, with multiple criteria. Choose one criterion and you may well [16] others. Everything can be done faster and made cheaper, but there is a [17] . Setting targets can and does have unforeseen negative consequences.
paragraphs.zh: 这个故事的寓意很简单。大多数工作都是多维度的,有多个标准。选择一个标准,你很可能会牺牲其他标准。一切都可以做得更快、成本更低,但这是有代价的。设定目标可能而且确实会产生意想不到的负面后果。

paragraphs.en: This is not an argument against target-setting. But it is an argument for exploring consequences first. All good targets should have multiple criteria [18] critical factors such as time, money, quality and customer feedback. The trick is not only to [19] just one or even two dimensions of the objective, but also to understand how to help people better [20] the objective.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不是反对设定目标的论点。但这是一个主张首先探讨后果的论点。所有好的目标都应该有与时间、金钱、质量和客户反馈等关键因素相关的多个标准。诀窍不仅在于只明确目标的一个甚至两个维度,还在于理解如何帮助人们更好地实现目标。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: People often complain that plastics are too durable. Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are everywhere and don't break down easily. But some plastic materials change over time. They crack and frizzle. They "weep" out additives. They melt into sludge. All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects. The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart. Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE). "It's like baking a cake: If you don't have exact amounts, it goes wrong," she says. "The object you make is already a time bomb." And sometimes, it's not the artist's fault. In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces. Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen "nature carpets"—large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons. He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets—which meant they had to be durable. Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable. It's especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi's pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling. Museums locked some of them away in the dark. So van Oosten and colleagues worked to preserve Gilardi's sculptures. They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals. Van Oosten calls those chemicals "sunscreens" because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers. She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases. Despite success stories like van Oosten's, preservation of plastics will likely get harder. Old objects continue to deteriorate. Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common. And more is at stake here than individual objects. Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums. We now live in an age of plastic, she says, "and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve…will have a strong impact on how in the future we'll be seen."

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey. Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued. Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries. This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available. Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset. Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles. For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two. It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable. It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory. Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: 'I am a geographer' or 'I am a classicist'. Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.

B) be diligent at each educational stage.
C) reassess the necessity of college education.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是推断题，正确答案 C）reassess the necessity of college education. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（a degree is not for everyone ↔ reassess the necessity of college education；other options are available ↔ reassess the necessity of college education）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The percentage of UK graduates in non-graduate roles reflects____
options: B) the shrinking value of a degree.
D) the desired route of social mobility.
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 B）the shrinking value of a degree. 定位句在第 2 段：但这一承诺已被发现落空。随着学位变得普及，它们也随之贬值。教育不再是社会流动的稳妥途径。如今，英国 28% 的毕业生在做非毕业生岗位，这一比例是 OECD 国家平均值的两倍。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they became devalued ↔ the shrinking value of a degree）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author considers it a good sign that____
options: A) Generation Z are seeking to earn a decent degree.
B) school leavers are willing to be skilled workers.
C) employers are taking a realistic attitude to degree.
D) parents are changing their minds about education.
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 C）employers are taking a realistic attitude to degree. 定位句在第 4 段：雇主们早已看到雇用高中毕业生的好处——他们往往比大学毕业生更敬业、更忠诚；许多雇主也开始看到取消某些岗位学位要求的好处。正确项与原文构成同义替换（scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles ↔ employers are taking a realistic attitude to degree；Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers ↔ employers are taking a realistic attitude to degree）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It is advised in Paragraph 5 that those with one degree should____
options: A) make an early decision on their career.
C) team up with high-paid postgraduates.
D) further their studies in a specific field.
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 D）further their studies in a specific field. 定位句在第 5 段：在通才横行的时代，掌握具体的知识或技能很值钱。研究生现在比本科生多挣 40%。当越来越多的人都有学位时，拥有两个学位就成了合理之举。正确项与原文构成同义替换（specific knowledge or skills ↔ further their studies in a specific field；it makes sense to have two ↔ further their studies）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can be concluded about Generation Z from the last two paragraphs?
options: A) Lifelong learning will define them.
B) They will make qualified educators.
C) Degrees will no longer appeal to them.
D) They will have a limited choice of jobs.
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是推断题，正确答案 A）Lifelong learning will define them. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable ↔ Lifelong learning will define them；their degree won't define them in the same way ↔ Lifelong learning will define them）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属过度推断、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
paragraphs.zh: 随着最新一批学生填写本科申请表并权衡他们的选择,或许值得考虑一下学位的意义、目的和价值是如何变化的,以及Z世代在开始其教育旅程的第三阶段时需要考虑什么。

paragraphs.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued. Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
paragraphs.zh: 千禧一代被告知,如果你在学校表现良好,获得一个体面的学位,你就会终身无忧。但这一承诺已被证明是不够的。随着学位变得普遍,它们也变得贬值了。教育不再是社会流动的可靠途径。如今,英国28%的大学毕业生从事非大学毕业生岗位,这一比例是OECD国家平均水平的两倍。

paragraphs.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不是说获得学位毫无意义,而是要强调学位并非适合每个人,从教室到讲堂的转变并非不可避免,还有其他选择可供选择。

paragraphs.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset. Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
paragraphs.zh: 值得庆幸的是,有迹象表明这种情况已经在发生,Z世代正在寻求从他们的千禧一代前辈那里学习,尽管父母和教师往往仍然固守学位思维模式。雇主早就看到了雇用高中毕业生的优势,这些人往往证明自己比大学毕业生更敬业和忠诚。许多雇主也看到了取消某些岗位学位要求的好处。

paragraphs.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
paragraphs.zh: 对于那些将学位作为理想路径的人来说,要考虑到这很可能是众多学位中的第一个。在这个通才的时代,拥有特定的知识或技能是值得的。研究生现在比本科生多挣40%。当我们越来越多的人拥有学位时,拥有两个学位就变得合理了。

paragraphs.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable. It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
paragraphs.zh: Z世代不太可能在18岁或21岁时就结束教育;他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能以保持就业能力。据估计,由于技术压力、个人成就感的愿望以及对多样性的渴望,这一代人在其职业生涯中将为17个不同的雇主工作,并拥有五种不同的职业。教育,而不仅仅是在校园获得的知识,将成为Z世代职业轨迹的核心部分。

paragraphs.en: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: 'I am a geographer' or 'I am a classicist'. Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.
paragraphs.zh: 老一辈人经常用现在时和个人化的方式谈论他们的学位:'我是一名地理学家'或'我是一名古典学家'。他们的儿女永远不会这样说;似乎他们已经知道自己的学位不会以同样的方式定义他们。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun. These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers. Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future. Such an encouraging result is not surprising. Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences. "Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning," one respondent said. One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK. But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street. Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements. Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study. The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work. Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art. More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture. The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the "visual studies" in the name. Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration. As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa. Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge. The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other. Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, art-science collaborations have____
options: A) caught the attention of critics.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 B）received favorable responses. 定位句在第 1 段：启发性强、富有挑战、引人思考、有趣。这些是《自然》杂志读者在一系列关于艺术家与研究者合作的文章中用来描述其艺-科合作体验的一些词。在约 350 位回应配套民调的人里，近 40% 表示自己曾与艺术家合作；几乎所有人都表示未来愿意尝试合作。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun ↔ favorable responses；almost all said they would consider doing so in future ↔ received favorable responses）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The reworked version of The Four Seasons is mentioned to show that____
options: A) art can offer audiences easy access to science.
B) science can help with the expression of emotions.
C) public participation in science has a promising future.
D) art is effective in facilitating scientific innovations.
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）art can offer audiences easy access to science. 定位句在第 3 段：上个月，悉尼交响乐团演奏了维瓦尔第《四季》的改编版，这是艺术家和科学家共同震撼舞台的一个例子。他们把莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的最新各季气候预测数据注入这部 300 年前的乐谱，重新构想了它。此次演出是 11 月格拉斯哥联合国气候变化大会前的一次极具创意的行动号召。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Artists help scientists reach a broader audience ↔ art can offer audiences easy access to science；make emotional connections that enhance learning ↔ easy access to science；injecting the latest climate prediction data ↔ art ... access to science）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属过度推断、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Some artists seem to worry about in the art-science partnership____
options: A) their role may be underestimated.
B) their reputation may be impaired.
C) their creativity may be inhibited.
D) their work may be misguided.
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 A）their role may be underestimated. 定位句在第 4 段：但真正的合作关系必须是双向的。回应《自然》民调的艺术家少于科学家；不过，一些受访者指出，艺术家不只是协助科学家完成传播任务。他们的作品也不应仅被当作研究对象。正确项与原文构成同义替换（artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements ↔ their role may be underestimated；Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study ↔ their role may be underestimated）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author say about CAYS?
options: A) It was headed alternately by artists and scientists.
B) It exemplified valuable art-science alliances.
C) Its projects aimed at advancing visual studies.
D) Its founders sought to raise the status of artists.
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 B）It exemplified valuable art-science alliances. 定位句在第 5 段：半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院创办了"先进视觉研究中心"（CAVS），以探索技术在文化中的角色。创办者刻意把项目聚焦在"光"上——所以名字里有"视觉研究"。光是艺术家和科学家都感兴趣的事物，因此能成为他们合作的基础。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration ↔ It exemplified valuable art-science alliances；looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa ↔ valuable art-science alliances）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author holds that art-science collaborations ____
options: A) are likely to go beyond public expectations.
C) should do more than communicating science.
D) are becoming more popular than before.
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是主旨题，正确答案 C）should do more than communicating science. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication ↔ should do more than communicating science；participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other ↔ should do more than communicating science）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun. These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers. Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
paragraphs.zh: 启迪人心、富有挑战、激发灵感、趣味盎然。这些是Nature读者在一系列关于艺术家与研究人员合作的文章中用来描述他们艺术-科学合作体验的词汇。在随附调查中,大约350名受访者中近40%的人表示他们曾与艺术家合作;几乎所有人都表示未来会考虑这样做。

paragraphs.en: Such an encouraging result is not surprising. Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences. "Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning," one respondent said.
paragraphs.zh: 如此令人鼓舞的结果并不令人意外。科学家们越来越多地寻求视觉艺术家帮助他们向新受众传播其工作。一位受访者说:"艺术家帮助科学家触及更广泛的受众,并建立情感联系以增强学习效果。"

paragraphs.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
paragraphs.zh: 上个月,艺术家与科学家如何共同震撼舞台的一个例子出现了,当时悉尼交响乐团演奏了Antonio Vivaldi《四季》的改编版本。他们通过注入Monash大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的每个季节的最新气候预测数据,重新构思了这部有300年历史的乐谱。这场演出是在英国格拉斯哥11月联合国气候变化大会之前发出的创意行动号召。

paragraphs.en: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street. Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements. Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study. The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work. Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.
paragraphs.zh: 但真正的合作伙伴关系必须是双向的。参与Nature调查的艺术家少于科学家;然而,几位受访者指出,艺术家不仅仅是协助科学家完成其传播需求。他们的作品也不应仅被视为研究对象。当科学家和艺术家在项目中拥有共同利益、能够共同设计项目并能够批评彼此的工作时,这种联盟最有价值。这种方法既可以激发新的研究,也可以产生有力的艺术作品。

paragraphs.en: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture. The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the "visual studies" in the name. Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration. As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
paragraphs.zh: 半个多世纪前,Massachusetts Institute of Technology开设了其高级视觉研究中心(CAVS),以探索技术在文化中的作用。创始人有意将他们的项目聚焦于光——因此名称中有"视觉研究"。光是艺术家和科学家都感兴趣的东西,因此可以构成合作的基础。随着科学技术的进步并细分为更多子学科,该中心同时展望着这样一个时代:顶尖研究人员也可以是艺术家、作家和诗人,反之亦然。

paragraphs.en: Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge. The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other. Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
paragraphs.zh: Nature的调查结果表明,这一趋势一如既往地强劲,但要使合作成功,双方都需要投入时间,并接受意外和挑战。艺术-科学合作的范围需要超越研究传播的必要目的,参与者不能陷入相互刻板印象的陷阱。艺术家和科学家都沉浸在发现和发明中,挑战和批判也是两者的核心。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause. Instead, dismissals must be justified. Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way. Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from "unjustified dismissals". The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management. Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice. But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives. As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance. The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure. Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them. Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal. Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk. If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages. Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record. Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA'S unjustified dismissal procedures. Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff. This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment. And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong. Society also suffers from excessive employment protections. Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being. Across the Tasman Sea, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws. In New Zealand, a 2016 private members' Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime. However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.

questions.stem: The personal grievance provisions of the ERA are intended to____
options: C) exempt employers from certain duties.
D) protect the rights of ordinary workers.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 D）protect the rights of ordinary workers. 定位句在第 2 段：人事申诉程序的设立目的，是保护普通工人的岗位免遭「不公正解雇」。正确项与原文构成同义替换（guard the jobs of ordinary workers ↔ protect the rights of ordinary workers；ordinary workers ↔ ordinary workers）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that the provisions may____
options: C) affect the public image of the firms.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是推断题，正确答案 A）hinder business development. 定位句在第 3 段：约束企业解雇业绩差、薪资高的管理者，是阻碍生产率与整体绩效提升的手刹。正确项与原文构成同义替换（a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance ↔ hinder business development；create difficulties for businesses ↔ hinder business development）。其余三项中，B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following measures would the Productivity Commission support?
options: C) Limiting the powers of business owners.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是推断题，正确答案 D）Dismissing poorly performing managers. 定位句在第 5 段：生产率委员会单独点名「管理能力低下」是新西兰生产率增长记录差的一大成因。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the low quality of managerial capabilities ↔ Dismissing poorly performing managers；as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record ↔ Dismissing poorly performing managers）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What might be an effect of ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures?
options: A) Highly paid managers lose their jobs.
B) Employees suffer from salary cuts.
C) Society sees a rise in overall well-being.
D) Employers need to hire new staff.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 B）Employees suffer from salary cuts. 定位句在第 5 段：即便不至于把岗位置于风险，只要用工保护法约束了企业主解雇业绩差的管理者，这些法律就成了企业生产率的束缚，进而压低了工人的工资。正确项与原文构成同义替换（therefore on workers' wages ↔ Employees suffer from salary cuts；firms pay staff less ↔ Employees suffer from salary cuts）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that the "high-income threshold" in Australia____
options: C) is beneficial to business owners.
D) is difficult to put into practice
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是推断题，正确答案 C）is beneficial to business owners. 定位句在第 8 段：澳大利亚处理这一不公正解雇悖论的办法，是把收入高于特定「高收入门槛」的雇员排除在不公平解雇法的保护范围之外。正确项与原文构成同义替换（excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws ↔ is beneficial to business owners；constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance ↔ is beneficial to business owners）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属张冠李戴、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause. Instead, dismissals must be justified. Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.
paragraphs.zh: 新西兰《2000年雇佣关系法》(ERA)的个人申诉条款禁止雇主无正当理由解雇员工。相反,解雇必须是正当的。雇主必须既要说明理由,又要以程序公正的方式行事。

paragraphs.en: Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from "unjustified dismissals". The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management. Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.
paragraphs.zh: 个人申诉程序旨在保护普通工人的工作免受"不正当解雇"的影响。其前提是合同普通法对工人缺乏足够的保障措施以防范管理层的武断行为。雇主只需给员工合同通知就能解雇的日子早已一去不复返。

paragraphs.en: But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives. As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance. The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure. Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them. Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.
paragraphs.zh: 但是,当这些条款适用于高薪经理和高管时,会给企业带来困难。正如无数董事会和企业主所证实的那样,限制公司解雇表现不佳、收入高的经理,是提高生产率和整体业绩的障碍。C级经理和A级经理之间的差异很可能就是企业成功或失败的差异。是保住普通工人的工作还是失去他们的工作。然而,平庸已不再足以成为解雇的正当理由。

paragraphs.en: Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
paragraphs.zh: 因此——也很矛盾的是——为保护普通工人工作而引入的法律可能正在使这些工作面临风险。

paragraphs.en: If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages. Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.
paragraphs.zh: 如果不是使工作面临风险,那么在雇佣保护法限制企业主解雇表现不佳的经理的程度上,这些法律就成为对企业生产率的约束,因而也是对工人工资的约束。事实上,在《新西兰生产率悖论的国际视角》(2014)中,生产率委员会特别指出管理能力的低质量是该国生产率增长记录不佳的一个原因。

paragraphs.en: Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA'S unjustified dismissal procedures. Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff. This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment. And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 高薪经理本身也不能免受ERA不正当解雇程序所造成的损害。由于雇佣保护法使解雇员工的成本更高,雇主在雇用新员工时更加谨慎。这使得边际经理更难获得就业。而且企业支付给员工的薪酬更少,因为企业承担着雇佣安排出错的负担。

paragraphs.en: Society also suffers from excessive employment protections. Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 社会也受到过度雇佣保护的损害。严格的工作解雇法规对生产率增长产生不利影响,并阻碍繁荣和整体福祉。

paragraphs.en: Across the Tasman Sea, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws. In New Zealand, a 2016 private members' Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime. However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.
paragraphs.zh: 在塔斯曼海对岸,澳大利亚通过将收入超过特定"高收入门槛"的员工排除在其不公平解雇法的保护之外,来应对不正当解雇悖论。在新西兰,2016年一项议员个人提案试图允许企业和高收入员工退出不正当解雇制度。然而,提议的机制繁琐不堪,该法案在当年晚些时候政府更迭后被否决。
