reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park? But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling. But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service. Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life. The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks. The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life. The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.

paragraphs.en: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?
paragraphs.zh: 联邦政府为弥补我们国家公园长期资金缺口而提出的想法很容易被视为荒谬。真的有人认为允许亚马逊将货物送到你在约塞米蒂的帐篷里，或者让餐车在红杉国家公园的红杉树下排成行是个好主意吗？

paragraphs.en: But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.
paragraphs.zh: 但政府在一件事上是对的：美国国家公园正处于危机之中。它们总共积压了超过120亿美元的维护费用。道路、小径、卫生间、游客中心和其他基础设施正在破败。

paragraphs.en: But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.
paragraphs.zh: 但将露营地私有化和商业化并不是万能药。露营地只占整体基础设施积压的很小一部分，而且公园内的企业平均只向国家公园管理局上交其收入的约5%。

paragraphs.en: Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，私有化程度的提高肯定会削弱每年3亿游客来公园的一个主要原因：享受自然，从充斥日常生活的商业鼓噪中得到喘息。

paragraphs.en: The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.
paragraphs.zh: 真正的问题是公园长期以来一直资金匮乏。一项针对700名美国纳税人的经济调查发现，人们愿意支付大量金钱以确保公园及其项目保持完整。约81%的受访者表示，他们愿意在未来10年缴纳额外税款，以避免国家公园遭受任何削减。

paragraphs.en: The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life.
paragraphs.zh: 国家公园作为逃离之地和自然象征，为美国居民提供了巨大价值。除此之外，它们还通过广泛的教育项目、通过碳封存对气候产生的积极影响、对我们文化和艺术生活的贡献，当然还有旅游业，创造价值。这些公园还帮助保持美国历史的鲜活，与全国数千个地方司法管辖区合作保护历史遗址，并让这些地方的故事生动起来。

paragraphs.en: The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.
paragraphs.zh: 公园以极少的预算完成所有这些工作。国会每年只拨款30亿美元给国家公园系统——这一数额自2001年以来一直持平（按通胀调整后的美元计算），除了2009年的一次性增加。与此同时，年游客数量自1980年以来增长了50%以上，现在达到每年3.3亿游客。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer ("an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain," for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but "adapting to new communications technology," Sparrow says. In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as "cognitive offloading." Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet. "I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things," Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it. Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles. "There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I'd have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs," observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. "It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don't know."

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Teenagers are paradoxical. That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers. A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand. The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence. For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved. The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk. The researchers studied "prosocial" and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old. The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late. Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older. But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly helping a friend. Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together. Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call "reward sensitivity." Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs. "Reward sensitivity" measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk. Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you. Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.

questions.stem: What is the text mainly about?
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）Why teenagers are self-contradictory. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Teenagers are paradoxical ↔ Why teenagers are self-contradictory；Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? ↔ Why；The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together ↔ self-contradictory）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Teenagers are paradoxical. That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.
paragraphs.zh: 青少年是矛盾的。这是一种温和而超然的说法,而父母们在表达同样的意思时往往会使用强烈得多的语言。但这种矛盾既是科学的,也是个人的。在青春期,几乎所有事情都依赖成年人的无助和依赖的儿童变成了能够照顾自己并互相帮助的独立个体。与此同时,曾经快乐顺从的孩子变成了叛逆的冒险少年。

paragraphs.en: A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand. The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence. For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved. The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.
paragraphs.zh: 莱顿大学的Eveline Crone及其同事在《儿童发展》期刊上发表的一项新研究表明,青少年的积极面和消极面是相伴而生的。这项研究是关于青春期思考新浪潮的一部分。长期以来,科学家和政策制定者专注于青少年是一个需要解决的问题这一观念。新的研究强调青春期既是机遇期也是风险期。

paragraphs.en: The researchers studied "prosocial" and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old. The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员对200多名年龄从11岁到28岁的儿童和年轻成人的亲社会特质和叛逆特质进行了研究。参与者填写了关于他们做利他和积极的事情(如牺牲自己的利益去帮助朋友)或叛逆和消极的事情(如喝醉或深夜不归)频率的问卷。

paragraphs.en: Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older. But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly helping a friend.
paragraphs.zh: 其他研究表明,叛逆行为在进入青少年时期时增加,然后随着年龄增长而减弱。但这项新研究显示,有趣的是,亲社会行为也呈现出同样的模式。青少年比年幼的儿童或成年人更有可能报告他们会做无私地帮助朋友之类的事情。

paragraphs.en: Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.
paragraphs.zh: 最重要的是,亲社会性和叛逆性之间存在正相关关系。越叛逆的青少年也越有可能帮助他人。青春期的好坏两面似乎是共同发展的。

paragraphs.en: Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call "reward sensitivity." Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs. "Reward sensitivity" measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.
paragraphs.zh: 是否存在某种共同因素作为这些看似矛盾的发展的基础?一种观点认为青少年行为与研究人员所说的奖赏敏感性有关。决策总是涉及平衡奖赏与风险、收益与成本。奖赏敏感性衡量的是需要多大的奖赏才能超过风险。

paragraphs.en: Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you. Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.
paragraphs.zh: 青少年对社会奖赏特别敏感——赢得比赛、给新朋友留下深刻印象、让那个男孩注意到你。奖赏敏感性和亲社会行为及冒险行为一样,似乎在青春期上升,然后随着我们年龄增长而再次下降。不知何故,当你到了30岁,那个聚会上可能会发生令人兴奋的新鲜事的机会似乎就不足以抵消从沙发上起身的努力了。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things. The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel. Why had the Romans buried a million nails? The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron. The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia. Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith's labour in a nail even more than the raw material. As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate. This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes. The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was. The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper. According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails. Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much. Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails. It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense. I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price. I am an economist, after all. After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world. The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper. Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.

questions.stem: The Romans buried the nails probably for the sake of______.
options: A) saving them for future use
C) letting them grow in value
D) hiding them from the locals
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 D）hiding them from the locals 定位句在第 2 段：最可能的解释是，撤退仓促，他们不想让当地的凯尔多尼亚人拿到这 10 吨可作武器原料的铁。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron ↔ hiding them from the locals）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、C 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The example of early 17th-century Virginians is used to______.
options: A) highlight the thriftiness of early American colonists
B) illustrate the high status of blacksmiths in that period
C) contrast the attitudes of different civilisations towards nails
D) show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是例证目的题，正确答案 D）show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time 定位句在第 3 段：「为了回收钉子竟然可能把整栋房子烧掉」这一想法，凸显出这项看似简单的技术当时是何等稀缺、昂贵、珍贵。正确项与原文构成同义替换（underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was ↔ show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: What played the major role in lowering the price of nails after the late 1700s?
options: B) Wider use of new energies.
D) Reduced cost of raw materials.
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 A）Increased productivity. 定位句在第 4 段：根据 Sichel 的研究，虽然钉子价格下降部分得益于铁和能源变便宜，但主要功劳归于钉子制造商，他们找到了把钢转为钉子的更高效方法。正确项与原文构成同义替换（nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails ↔ Increased productivity）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 5 that nails______.
options: A) have undergone many technological improvements
B) have remained basically the same since Roman times
C) are less studied than other everyday products
D) are one of the world's most significant inventions
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 B）have remained basically the same since Roman times 定位句在第 5 段：钉子本身这些年也有变化，但 Sichel 研究它们恰因为它们变化不大。罗马的灯具和马车与 LED 灯带和跑车截然不同，但罗马的钉子至今仍明显就是钉子。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Roman nails are still clearly nails ↔ have remained basically the same since Roman times；they haven't changed much ↔ have remained basically the same since Roman times）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarises the last two paragraphs?
options: A) Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change.
B) Technological innovation is integral to economic success.
C) Technology defines people's understanding of the world.
D) Sophisticated technologies develop from small inventions.
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it's the cheap technologies that change the world ↔ Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change；Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system ↔ Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属答非所问、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things. The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
paragraphs.zh: 将近2000年前,当罗马人开始撤出苏格兰时,他们留下了一件奇特的宝藏:10吨钉子,将近一百万枚。这批钉子宝藏于1960年在一个四米深的坑中被发现,坑上覆盖着两米厚的砾石。

paragraphs.en: Why had the Romans buried a million nails? The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron. The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
paragraphs.zh: 罗马人为何要埋藏一百万枚钉子?最可能的解释是撤军过于仓促,他们不想让当地的喀里多尼亚人得到这10吨可用作武器的铁。罗马人把钉子埋得如此之深,以至于它们在近两千年后才被发现。

paragraphs.en: Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith's labour in a nail even more than the raw material. As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate. This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes. The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
paragraphs.zh: 后来的文明更加看重熟练铁匠在一枚钉子上付出的劳动,甚至超过原材料本身的价值。正如Roma Agrawal在她令人愉悦的新书《螺母与螺栓》中所解释的,17世纪早期的弗吉尼亚人如果打算搬迁,有时会烧毁自己的房屋。这是为了回收那些珍贵的钉子,它们可以在筛过灰烬后重新使用。为了回收钉子而烧毁整座房屋的做法,凸显了这种看似简单的技术是多么稀缺、昂贵和珍贵。

paragraphs.en: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper. According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
paragraphs.zh: 经济学家Daniel Sichel在一篇研究论文中指出,从18世纪末到20世纪中期,钉子的价格下降了90%。根据Sichel的研究,尽管钉子价格的下降部分是由更便宜的铁和更便宜的能源推动的,但大部分功劳应归于钉子制造商,他们只是找到了将钢铁变成钉子的更高效方法。

paragraphs.en: Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much. Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails. It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense.
paragraphs.zh: 钉子本身多年来有所变化,但Sichel研究它们是因为它们变化不大。罗马灯具和罗马战车与LED灯带和跑车截然不同,但罗马钉子显然仍是钉子。试图追踪自1695年以来跑车价格的变化是荒谬的,但对钉子提出同样的问题则完全合理。

paragraphs.en: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price. I am an economist, after all. After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world.
paragraphs.zh: 我对日常物品的一个特定特征着迷,对此我不作任何辩解:它们的价格。毕竟,我是一名经济学家。在撰写了两本关于发明史的书之后,我学到的一点是,尽管那些迷人而复杂的技术获得了所有的炒作,但改变世界的是廉价技术。

paragraphs.en: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper. Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.
paragraphs.zh: 古腾堡印刷机改变了文明,不是通过改变书写的本质,而是通过改变其成本——如果没有书写表面价格的同步暴跌,它不会取得多大成就,这要归功于一种常被忽视的技术,叫做纸张。太阳能电池板在变得廉价之前只有少数利基用途;现在它们正在改变全球能源系统。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested. The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults. Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones and "baby-wearing", in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm. According to Dr. Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents. Dr. Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life. In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people's home with a nursery. The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting. Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years to mirror the unsupervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities. In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history. This abrupt shift to an "intensive mothering narrative", which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful. "Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences," they wrote. By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child's care. One previous study looked at the Efé people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour. Chaudhary said that parents now had less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans' evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to a child's wellbeing. An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers—this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three. While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents "might also enhance their own social development".

The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting. paragraphs.en: In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history. This abrupt shift to an "intensive mothering narrative", which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful. "Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences," they wrote.
paragraphs.zh: 在发表于《儿童心理学与精神病学杂志》的一篇论文中,研究人员表示,西方核心家庭是一项与进化史决裂的近期发明。这种突然转向"密集型母职叙事"的做法很可能是有害的,这种叙事认为母亲应该独自承担育儿责任。他们写道:"这种叙事会导致母亲精疲力竭,并产生危险的后果。"

paragraphs.en: By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child's care. One previous study looked at the Efé people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下,在狩猎采集社会中,父母以外的成年人可以提供儿童近一半的照料。此前一项研究考察了刚果民主共和国的Efé人。研究发现,婴儿在18周大时平均每天有14个异亲抚育者,每小时在照顾者之间传递八次。

paragraphs.en: Chaudhary said that parents now had less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans' evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to a child's wellbeing. An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers—this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.
paragraphs.zh: Chaudhary表示,与人类进化史的大部分时期相比,父母现在从家庭和社会网络获得的育儿支持更少,但引入额外的照顾者可以减少压力和产妇抑郁,这可能对儿童的健康产生"连锁"效益。在狩猎采集社会中出生的婴儿可能有十多个照顾者——这与英国的托儿所环境形成鲜明对比,英国的规定要求一名照顾者对应四名两到三岁的儿童。

paragraphs.en: While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents "might also enhance their own social development".
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,虽然狩猎采集者儿童通过在混龄游戏小组中的观察和模仿来学习,但西方的"指导式教学",即要求学生坐着不动,可能会导致注意力缺陷多动障碍等疾病。Chaudhary表示,英国应该探索这样一种可能性:年长的兄弟姐妹帮助父母"也可能促进他们自己的社会发展"。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: A Polish digital artist who uses classical painting styles to create dreamy fantasy landscapes, Greg Rutkowski has made illustrations for games such as Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering. And he's become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation. His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion. The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts. For example, type in "Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski," and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski's style. But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the Internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists. As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright. And artists like Rutkowski have had enough. According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million Stable Diffusion images and prompts, Rutkowski's name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times. Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences. Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published. The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn't his. "It's been just a month. What about in a year? I probably won't be able to find my work out there because the Internet will be flooded with AI art," Rutkowski said. "That's concerning." Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in text-to-image generators—and some are now fighting back. Karla Ortiz, an illustrator based in San Francisco who found her work in Stable Diffusion's data set, has been raising awareness about the issues around AI art and copyright. Artists say they risk losing income as people start using AI-generated images based on copyrighted material for commercial purposes. But it's also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that because art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems. "There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this," says Ortiz. The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation. One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.

The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts. For example, type in "Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski," and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski's style.
paragraphs.zh: 他的独特风格现在已成为新开源AI艺术生成器Stable Diffusion中最常用的提示词之一。该工具与其他流行的图像生成AI模型一样，允许任何人根据文本提示创建令人印象深刻的图像。例如，输入"手持剑和魔法火球的巫师与凶猛的龙战斗 Greg Rutkowski"，系统就会生成看起来与Rutkowski风格的作品相差不远的东西。

paragraphs.en: But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the Internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists. As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright. And artists like Rutkowski have had enough.
paragraphs.zh: 但这些开源程序是通过从互联网上抓取图像构建的，通常未经许可，也没有对艺术家进行适当署名。因此，它们引发了关于伦理和版权的棘手问题。像Rutkowski这样的艺术家已经受够了。

paragraphs.en: According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million Stable Diffusion images and prompts, Rutkowski's name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times. Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences. Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published. The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn't his.
paragraphs.zh: 根据追踪超过1000万张Stable Diffusion图像和提示词的网站Lexica，Rutkowski的名字已被用作提示词约93000次。Rutkowski最初感到惊讶，但认为这可能是接触新受众的好方法。然后他尝试搜索自己的名字，看看他参与制作的作品是否已发布。网络搜索带回了带有他名字但并非他创作的作品。

paragraphs.en: "It's been just a month. What about in a year? I probably won't be able to find my work out there because the Internet will be flooded with AI art," Rutkowski said. "That's concerning."
paragraphs.zh: "这才过了一个月。一年后会怎样?我可能将无法在网上找到自己的作品，因为互联网将被AI艺术淹没，"Rutkowski说。"这令人担忧。"

paragraphs.en: Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in text-to-image generators—and some are now fighting back.
paragraphs.zh: 除Rutkowski之外的其他艺术家也对他们的作品在文本生成图像生成器中的明显流行度感到惊讶——其中一些人现在正在反击。

paragraphs.en: Karla Ortiz, an illustrator based in San Francisco who found her work in Stable Diffusion's data set, has been raising awareness about the issues around AI art and copyright. Artists say they risk losing income as people start using AI-generated images based on copyrighted material for commercial purposes. But it's also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that because art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems.
paragraphs.zh: Karla Ortiz是一位驻旧金山的插画家，她在Stable Diffusion的数据集中发现了自己的作品，一直在提高人们对AI艺术和版权相关问题的认识。艺术家们表示，随着人们开始将基于受版权保护材料的AI生成图像用于商业目的，他们面临失去收入的风险。但Ortiz说，这也更具个人性，她认为由于艺术与个人联系如此紧密，它可能会引发数据保护和隐私问题。

paragraphs.en: "There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this," says Ortiz. The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation. One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.
paragraphs.zh: "艺术家行业内正在形成一个联盟，以弄清如何应对或缓解这一问题，"Ortiz说。该组织处于动员的早期阶段，可能涉及推动新政策或法规。Ortiz说，一个建议是AI模型可以在公共领域的图像上进行训练，AI公司可以与博物馆和艺术家建立合作关系。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction, the interaction of fresh and saline waters, and the mix of land and water. The shallows provide homes for hundreds of species while storing floodwaters, filtering pollutants from water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges. All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways. Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a "continuous surface connection" to bodies of water. This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules. And it carries "significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States," as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed. In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections. But that's a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay. The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don't respect state boundaries. The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware. Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v. EPA? Perhaps some, but all? That seems unlikely. It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors. And it's a reminder that the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states. Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream. And so we would call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved. We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them, but teeming with aquatic life. It's worth the scenic drive.

Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream.

It's worth the scenic drive.

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. "Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past," she writes. "An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable." Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can't be expected to embrace the changes if they're not seeing the benefits—if they're just seeing good jobs being destroyed. In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. "We're talking about disruption," she says. "These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed." To make such "tremendous changes," she adds, you need social buy-in. Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities. According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings's Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States. The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow. Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants. A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.

questions.stem: Coyle argues in her new book that economic growth should_______.
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 C）benefit people equally 定位句在第 1 段：无论我们所说的经济增长、事情变好是什么意思，收益都必须比近期更均衡地分享。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the gains will have to be more evenly shared ↔ benefit people equally）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, digital technologies should be used to_______.
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是细节题，正确答案 C）raise overall work efficiency 定位句在第 2 段：Coyle 说，要改善生活水平、让更多人富裕，就需要更广泛地使用数字技术，以提高包括医疗和建筑在内的多个行业的生产率。正确项与原文构成同义替换（boost productivity in various sectors ↔ raise overall work efficiency）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断、B 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does Coyle fear about transformative technologies?
options: A) They may affect work-life balance.
B) They may be impractical to deploy.
C) They may incur huge expenditure.
D) They may be unwelcome to the public.
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 D）They may be unwelcome to the public. 定位句在第 3 段：Coyle 说她担心科技业的不平等问题可能成为部署 AI 的障碍。……她补充说，要实现这种“巨大变革”，需要社会的认同。正确项与原文构成同义替换（you need social buy-in ↔ unwelcome to the public；tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI ↔ unwelcome to the public）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Several American cities are mentioned to show______.
options: A) the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US
B) the disappointing prospect of tech jobs in the US
C) the fast progress of US regional economies
D) the increasing significance of US AI assets
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US 定位句在第 5 段：据布鲁金斯学会，截至 2019 年，包括旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图在内的八座美国城市约占全部科技岗位的 38%。新 AI 技术尤其集中：布鲁金斯学会的 Mark Muro 和 Sifan Liu 估算，仅 15 座城市就占了美国 AI 资产与能力的三分之二。正确项与原文构成同义替换（New AI technologies are particularly concentrated ↔ the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US；just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States ↔ uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: With regard to Coyle's concern, the author suggests______.
options: A) raising funds to start new AI projects
B) encouraging collaboration in AI research
C) guarding against the side effects of AI
D) redefining the role of AI technologies
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是细节题，正确答案 D）redefining the role of AI technologies 定位句在第 8 段：更直接的应对是拓宽我们的数字想象力，去构想这样的 AI 技术：它们不只是替代岗位，而是在全国各地最在乎的领域——如医疗、教育和制造业——扩大机会。正确项与原文构成同义替换（broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities ↔ redefining the role of AI technologies）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. "Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past," she writes. "An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable."
paragraphs.zh: 在她的新书《齿轮与怪兽：经济学是什么，以及它应该是什么》中，剑桥大学经济学家Diane Coyle认为，数字经济需要关于进步的新思维方式。她写道："无论我们所说的经济增长、事物变得更好是什么意思,收益都必须比近期更加均匀地分享。一个由科技百万富翁或亿万富翁和零工工人组成的经济体,其中等收入工作被自动化削弱,将无法在政治上持续。"

paragraphs.en: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can't be expected to embrace the changes if they're not seeing the benefits—if they're just seeing good jobs being destroyed.
paragraphs.zh: Coyle说,提高生活水平和让更多人增加繁荣将需要更多地使用数字技术来提高包括医疗保健和建筑在内的各个部门的生产力。但如果人们看不到好处——如果他们只是看到好工作被摧毁,就不能期望他们接受这些变化。

paragraphs.en: In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. "We're talking about disruption," she says. "These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed." To make such "tremendous changes," she adds, you need social buy-in.
paragraphs.zh: 在最近的一次采访中,Coyle说她担心科技的不平等问题可能成为部署人工智能的障碍。她说:"我们谈论的是颠覆。这些是变革性技术,改变了我们每天度过时间的方式,改变了成功的商业模式。"她补充说,要做出这样的"巨大变化",你需要社会认同。

paragraphs.en: Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.
paragraphs.zh: Coyle说,相反,随着收益被认为流向少数繁荣城市的精英,许多人的怨恨正在酝酿。

paragraphs.en: According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings's Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States.
paragraphs.zh: 根据Brookings Institution的数据,到2019年,包括旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图在内的八个美国城市的简短名单拥有大约38%的科技工作岗位。新的人工智能技术尤其集中:Brookings的Mark Muro和Sifan Liu估计,仅15个城市就占据了美国三分之二的人工智能资产和能力。

paragraphs.en: The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.
paragraphs.zh: 少数城市在人工智能发明和商业化方面的主导地位意味着地理上的财富差距将继续飙升。这不仅会助长政治和社会动荡,而且正如Coyle所说,它可能阻碍区域经济增长所需的各种人工智能技术。

paragraphs.en: Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.
paragraphs.zh: 解决方案的一部分可能在于以某种方式放松大型科技公司对定义人工智能议程的控制。这可能需要增加联邦资金,用于独立于科技巨头的研究。

paragraphs.en: A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.
paragraphs.zh: 一个更直接的应对措施是拓宽我们的数字想象力,构想不是简单地取代工作而是在国家不同地区最关心的部门(如医疗保健、教育和制造业)扩大机会的人工智能技术。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country's reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world. Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don't go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. "Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood," said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. "For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall." The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent. The causes of the UK's current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels. It also encompasses significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects. While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall added: "While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero." "While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground. Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand."

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that the UK needs to______.
options: A) increase its domestic wood supply
B) reduce its demand for timber
C) lower its wood production costs
D) lift its control on timber imports
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 A）increase its domestic wood supply 定位句在第 1 段：目前英国仅有 20% 的木材需求由本土生产，而它仍是世界第二大木材净进口国。正确项与原文构成同义替换（only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown ↔ increase its domestic wood supply；home-grown ↔ domestic）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Confor, the UK government's fresh incentives______.
options: A) can hardly address a construction crisis
B) are believed to come at a wrong time
C) seem to be misleading for landowners
D) will be too costly to put into practice
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 A）can hardly address a construction crisis 定位句在第 2 段：在英国政府推出鼓励土地所有者多种树的新激励措施之时，这家行业组织（Confor）表示这些措施做得还不够，且未能宣传种树以增加木材供应的益处。正确项与原文构成同义替换（don't go far enough ↔ can hardly address a construction crisis；a future construction crisis ↔ a construction crisis）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The UK's exposure to fluctuating wood prices is a result of______.
options: A) the government's inaction on timber imports
B) inadequate investment in growing wood
C) the competition among timber traders at home
D) wood producers' motive to maximise profits
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 B）inadequate investment in growing wood 定位句在第 2 段：几十年来我们没有承担起投资本土木材供应的责任，这使我们暴露在波动的价格之下，并在全球需求上涨、本国供应下降之时争夺未来的木材供应。正确项与原文构成同义替换（have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply ↔ inadequate investment in growing wood；our domestic wood supply ↔ growing wood）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following causes the shortage of wood supply in the UK?
options: A) Excessive timber consumption in construction.
B) Unfavourable conditions for growing wood.
C) Outdated technologies of the wood industry.
D) Farmers' unwillingness to plant trees.
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 D）Farmers' unwillingness to plant trees. 定位句在第 3 段：造成英国目前处境的原因是复杂的，从对生产性林业的过时观念到灰松鼠对树木的毁灭性破坏不一而足；此外还包括农民和其他土地所有者对长期种植项目投资的显著犹豫。正确项与原文构成同义替换（significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects ↔ Farmers' unwillingness to plant trees；farmers and other landowners ↔ Farmers'）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does Goodall think the UK government should do?
options: A) Subsidise the building of low-carbon homes.
B) Pay greater attention to boosting rural economies.
C) Provide more support for productive tree planting.
D) Give priority to pursuing its net-zero strategy.
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是细节题，正确答案 C）Provide more support for productive tree planting. 定位句在第 4 段：尽管生产性的种树可以为农村经济带来实实在在的经济收益，并有助于英国的净零战略，但政府支持的重点仍放在粮食生产以及仅为生物多样性而进行的再野化和原生林种植上。正确项与原文构成同义替换（productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies ↔ Provide more support for productive tree planting；the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity ↔ Provide more support）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属以偏概全、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country's reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.
paragraphs.zh: Confor警告称,由于未能种植树木以生产木材,英国正面临未来的建筑危机。这家林业和木材贸易机构呼吁采取紧急行动,减少国家对木材进口的依赖,并为子孙后代提供稳定的木材供应。目前英国木材需求中仅有20%来自国内生产,而英国仍然是世界上第二大木材净进口国。

paragraphs.en: Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don't go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. "Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood," said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. "For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall."
paragraphs.zh: 在英国政府为土地所有者提供更多种树激励措施之际,该贸易机构表示这些措施力度不够,未能宣传种植树木以增加木材供应的好处。Confor首席执行官Stuart Goodall说:"我们现在不仅面临碳危机,而且由于未能种植树木以生产木材,我们还将面临未来的建筑危机。几十年来,我们没有承担起投资国内木材供应的责任,这使我们面临价格波动的风险,并在全球需求上升而我们自身供应下降之际争夺未来的木材供应。"

paragraphs.en: The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent. The causes of the UK's current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels. It also encompasses significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects.
paragraphs.zh: Confor表示,英国拥有种植木材以建造低碳住宅的理想条件,并且在认证其森林可持续管理方面处于全球领先地位。虽然约四分之三的苏格兰住宅使用苏格兰木材建造,但英格兰使用国产木材的比例仅约25%。英国当前处境的原因是复杂的,既包括对生产性林业的过时认知,也包括灰松鼠对树木的大量破坏。这还涉及农民和其他土地所有者对投资长期种植项目的明显犹豫。

paragraphs.en: While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall added: "While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero."
paragraphs.zh: 虽然生产性树木种植可以为农村经济带来实际的经济效益,并有助于英国的净零排放战略,但政府支持的重点仍然集中在粮食生产以及仅为生物多样性而进行的野化和本土林地种植。Goodall补充说:"虽然粮食生产和生物多样性健康显然至关重要,但我们需要土地也能提供用于建筑、制造的可靠木材供应,并为实现净零排放做出贡献。"

paragraphs.en: "While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground. Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand."
paragraphs.zh: "虽然英国政府已表明其扩大植树的雄心,但实际行动却很少。Confor现在呼吁为这些愿景注入更大的推动力,以确保我们有足够的木材来满足不断增长的需求。"

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it's time to turn over the keys. "It's a complete life-changer" when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke. "The American Medical Association advises physicians that 'in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician's advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,'" Menke wrote. "Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality," she counseled. Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. "There's not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies," she said. "We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe" and what can help, said Dugan. One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two. Many older drivers don't see eye doctors or can't afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven't changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily. As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won't solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. "If we're going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably."

questions.stem: According to Paragraph l, keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road______.
options: A) is a new safety measure
B) has become a disputed issue
C) can be a tough task to complete
D) will be beneficial to their health
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 C）can be a tough task to complete 定位句在第 1 段：让不安全的高龄司机远离道路，其最大挑战之一是说服他们：是时候交出车钥匙了。正确项与原文构成同义替换（One of the biggest challenges ↔ a tough task to complete）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The American Medical Association's advice______.
options: A) has won support from drivers
C) is widely dismissed as unnecessary
D) has met with different responses
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是细节题，正确答案 D）has met with different responses 定位句在第 2 段：一些州要求医生上报，另一些州允许但不强制上报，还有少数州把上报视为对保密义务的违反。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality ↔ met with different responses）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴、B 项属无中生有、C 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Dugan, efforts to keep older drivers safe______.
options: A) have brought about big changes
B) need to be well coordinated
D) call for relevant legal support
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 B）need to be well coordinated 定位句在第 3 段：Dugan 指出，保障老年司机安全的部分症结在于：这些难题正被不同专业、各执焦点地零碎应对，参与者包括老年学家、高速公路管理官员、汽车工程师等。正确项与原文构成同义替换（addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses ↔ need to be well coordinated）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Some older drivers have trouble driving because they tend to______.
options: A) stick with bad driving habits
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 B）have a weakened memory 定位句在第 5 段：初级保健医生分身乏术，可能无法跟进那些开车有困难的患者——这些患者要么不能转头、要么记不住自己要去哪儿，要么个子变矮了又没把座椅调到能轻松踩到踏板的位置。正确项与原文构成同义替换（can't ... remember where they are going ↔ have a weakened memory）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Dugan thinks that the solution to the problems of crashes may lie in______.
options: D) adjusting the age limit for drivers
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是细节题，正确答案 B）developing senior-friendly cars 定位句在第 6 段：但 Dugan 说，我们需要做更多事来提升安全。她说："如果我们都要活到 100 岁，那就需要 90 岁老人也能舒适驾驶的汽车。"正确项与原文构成同义替换（cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably ↔ developing senior-friendly cars）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it's time to turn over the keys. "It's a complete life-changer" when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.
paragraphs.zh: 让不安全的老年驾驶员远离道路的最大挑战之一是说服他们是时候交出钥匙了。前风险管理人员Anne M. Menke说,当有人停止驾驶或被迫停止驾驶时,"这完全改变了生活"。

paragraphs.en: "The American Medical Association advises physicians that 'in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician's advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,'" Menke wrote. "Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality," she counseled.
paragraphs.zh: Menke写道:"美国医学会建议医生,'在有明确证据表明存在严重驾驶障碍,对患者和公共安全构成重大威胁,且医生建议停止驾驶特权而被忽视的情况下,通知机动车辆管理部门是可取且合乎道德的。'一些州要求医生报告,另一些州允许但不强制要求报告,而少数州认为报告属于违反保密义务。如果医生的行为不符合州法律关于报告和保密的规定,可能会承担责任和处罚。"她建议道。

paragraphs.en: Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. "There's not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies," she said. "We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe" and what can help, said Dugan.
paragraphs.zh: 老年学家Elizabeth Dugan说,保护老年驾驶员安全的部分问题在于,这些困难被不同专业、不同关注点的人员零散地处理,包括老年学家、公路管理官员、汽车工程师等。"没有一个国家老年驾驶员研究所。"她说。Dugan说:"我们需要更好的证据来说明是什么让驾驶员不安全"以及什么能有所帮助。

paragraphs.en: One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.
paragraphs.zh: 一项研究显示,有一件事似乎确实有效,那就是要求驾驶员亲自到场更新驾照。强制性亲自更新与85岁或以上驾驶员涉及的致命车祸减少31%相关。通过视力测试也使这些驾驶员的致命车祸出现了类似的下降,尽管将两者结合起来似乎没有什么益处。

paragraphs.en: Many older drivers don't see eye doctors or can't afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven't changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily.
paragraphs.zh: 许多老年驾驶员不去看眼科医生或负担不起。初级保健提供者手头工作繁重,可能无法跟进那些因无法转头或记不住要去哪里而驾驶困难的患者,或者那些身高变矮却没有充分调整座椅设置以便轻松够到汽车踏板的患者。

paragraphs.en: As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won't solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. "If we're going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably."
paragraphs.zh: Dugan说,只要路上还有其他汽车,自动驾驶汽车就无法解决车祸问题。她说,避免所有那些人类驾驶员造成的危险需要太多算法。但Dugan说,我们需要做更多工作来提高安全性。"如果我们要活到100岁,我们需要90岁的人能够舒适驾驶的汽车。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone. While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections. Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that "despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties." Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained. Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is. As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.

questions.stem: The research findings are cited in Paragraph 1 to show______.
options: A) the prevalence of health apps
B) the public concern over health
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）the prevalence of health apps 定位句在第 1 段：来自 Care and Health Applications 评估组织的最新研究发现，市场上共有 350,000 款健康类应用，其中仅 2020 年就上市了 90,000 款。正确项与原文构成同义替换（350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone ↔ the prevalence of health apps；chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several ↔ health apps）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有=原文找不到对应、C 项属偷换概念=主语对象替换、D 项属过度推断=从数据跳到泛化结论，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author imply about existing health privacy law?
options: A) Its coverage needs to be extended.
C) It has discouraged medical misconduct.
D) It has disappointed insurance companies.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是推断题，正确答案 A）Its coverage needs to be extended. 定位句在第 2 段：现行的健康隐私法（例如《健康保险流通与责任法案》）主要管医院、诊所、保险公司在线保存病历的方式。而这些 app 和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备所收集的健康信息，通常得不到同等的法律保护。正确项与原文构成同义替换（is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online ↔ Its coverage；The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections ↔ needs to be extended）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有=换维度、C 项属无中生有=横插无关话题、D 项属张冠李戴=对象角色错位，均可排除。

questions.stem: Before sharing its users' health information, Flo Health is required to______.
options: A) seek the approval of the FTC
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 D）obtain their explicit permission 定位句在第 3 段：Flo Health 与 FTC 通过一份同意令了结此案：该同意令要求公司在分享用户健康信息之前必须获得用户明确肯定的同意，并要求其指示第三方删除已获取的数据。正确项与原文构成同义替换（get app users' express affirmative consent ↔ obtain their explicit permission）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴=同意主体错位、B 项属无中生有=蹭关键词造新要求、C 项属答非所问=时点错位，均可排除。

questions.stem: What challenge is the FTC currently faced with?
options: A) The complexity of health information.
B) The rapid increase in new health apps.
C) The subtle deceptiveness of health apps.
D) The difficulty in assessing consumer harm.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 B）The rapid increase in new health apps. 定位句在第 4 段：尽管 FTC 正在竭尽所能确保这些 app 兑现对消费者关于敏感健康信息处置的承诺，但这些健康 app 涌入市场的速度，显示出这一挑战何其巨大。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market ↔ The rapid increase in new health apps）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有=造新挑战维度、C 项属偷换概念=移位+加修饰、D 项属无中生有=蹭术语造新难点，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that health data protection______.
options: A) has been embraced by health app developers
B) has been a focus of federal policy-making
C) has encountered opposition in California
D) has gained legislative support in some states
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是推断题，正确答案 D）has gained legislative support in some states 定位句在第 5 段：至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为短期内全面的联邦隐私立法不太可能。各州已开始自行推出方案，加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。加州凭借 2018 年《加州消费者隐私法案》一直走在州一级隐私保护的最前列。弗吉尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他也最近通过了州一级的消费者数据隐私立法。正确项与原文构成同义替换（States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data ↔ has gained legislative support in some states；California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 ↔ legislative support；Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation ↔ in some states）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有=换主语角色、B 项属与原文相反=方向颠倒、C 项属与原文相反=立场颠倒，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你查看手机上的应用程序,很可能至少有一个与健康相关的应用——而且可能有好几个。无论是心理健康应用、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是其他什么,我们中的许多人都在利用这项技术以某种形式更好地追踪自己的健康状况。健康与护理应用审查组织最近的研究发现,市场上有35万个健康应用程序,其中仅2020年就推出了9万个。

paragraphs.en: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然这些应用程序有很多好处,但我们输入的个人信息如何被收集、保护和在线共享并不总是清楚的。现有的健康隐私法律,如《健康保险携带和责任法案》,主要关注医院、诊所、门诊部和保险公司在线存储健康记录的方式。这些应用程序和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备收集的健康信息通常不会受到同样的法律保护。

paragraphs.en: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that "despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties." Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
paragraphs.zh: 在没有额外保护措施的情况下,公司可能会以消费者未授权或未预料到的方式共享(并可能将其货币化)个人健康信息。2021年,Flo Health面临联邦贸易委员会的调查。联邦贸易委员会在一项投诉中指控"尽管有明确的隐私声明,该公司还是控制了用户的敏感生育数据并将其与第三方共享"。Flo Health与联邦贸易委员会通过一项同意令解决了此事,要求该公司在共享用户健康信息之前获得应用程序用户的明确肯定同意,并指示第三方删除他们已获得的数据。

paragraphs.en: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
paragraphs.zh: 《联邦贸易委员会法》第5条授权联邦贸易委员会对不公平或欺骗性行为采取执法行动,这意味着联邦贸易委员会只能在公司的隐私做法具有误导性或造成不正当消费者损害之后采取行动。虽然联邦贸易委员会正在尽其所能确保应用程序信守对消费者关于处理其敏感健康信息的承诺,但这些健康应用程序进入市场的速度表明这是一个多么巨大的挑战。

paragraphs.en: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
paragraphs.zh: 至于联邦立法的前景,评论人士认为短期内似乎不太可能出台全面的联邦隐私立法。各州已开始实施自己的解决方案,以加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。加利福尼亚州一直处于州隐私努力的前沿,制定了2018年《加利福尼亚州消费者隐私法》。弗吉尼亚州、科罗拉多州和犹他州最近也通过了州消费者数据隐私立法。

blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 C）whereas。同句左右两半呈正反对照。其余三项：A）because 错因：把 "对照" 误读成 "因果"、B）unless 错因：条件关系与原文无关、D）until 错因：时间界限与本句无关，均可排除。
