第 5 空正确答案 A）contribute to。loneliness 的负面效应链。其余三项：B）rely on 错因："依赖" 不符合主语角色、C）interfere with 错因：意为 "干扰"，与 a low mood 不搭、D）go against 错因：方向相反，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 C）for example。前句抽象、空后给出具体场景。其余三项：A）in fact 错因：常用于 "递进强调或反差"，与本句结构不符、B）of course 错因：表 "理所当然"，与举例不搭、D）on average 错因：表 "平均而言"，需要数据语境，均可排除。
第 7 空正确答案 B）missing out。+on 的常用搭配 + 上下文 "在家工作错失办公室寒暄"。其余三项：A）cutting back 错因：搭配多用 on 但意为 "削减"，主观能动、C）breaking in 错因：搭配与语义都不对、D）looking down 错因：look down on = 看不起，色彩负面，均可排除。
第 8 空正确答案 B）trigger。举例支持 "引发 → 孤独期"。其余三项：A）shorten 错因：方向相反、C）follow 错因：方向颠倒、D）interrupt 错因：意为 "打断"，与 "造成" 相反，均可排除。
第 9 空正确答案 D）regain。P3 提供 "重建社交" 的具体方法。其余三项：A）assess 错因："评估" 与后文具体行动不接、B）interpret 错因："解释" 不与 a social life 搭配、C）provide 错因：主体错位，均可排除。
第 10 空正确答案 A）at first。下一句紧接 "先从兴趣入手"——暗示 "起步阶段"。其余三项：B）in turn 错因："依次/反过来" 与本句逻辑无关、C）on time 错因：意为 "准时"，与情绪 overwhelming 不搭、D）by chance 错因："偶然" 与 "起步阶段" 无关，均可排除。
第 11 空正确答案 D）like-minded。前文提兴趣团体，下文列同好群体。其余三项：A）far-sighted 错因："有远见的" 与 "兴趣团体" 主线无关、B）strong-willed 错因："意志坚定" 与 "共同爱好" 不对应、C）kind-hearted 错因："好心" 偏品德，不指向 "共同兴趣"，均可排除。
第 12 空正确答案 A）try。for the first time 锁定 "首次尝试"。其余三项：B）promote 错因："推广" 主体错位、C）watch 错因："观看" 与 social life 主线不符、D）describe 错因："描述" 与 sport 搭配语义不通，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 B）share。networking events 目的=互通有无。其余三项：A）test 错因："测试" 偏实验/产品语境、C）accept 错因："接受" 单向，networking 是双向交流、D）revise 错因："修订" 缺前提，均可排除。
第 14 空正确答案 C）also。段首 On the other hand 暗示并列对立。其余三项：A）already 错因："已经" 表示时间完成，与 possible 不搭、B）thus 错因："因此" 表因果，与对照矛盾、D）only 错因："仅仅" 缩小范围，文意不符，均可排除。
第 15 空正确答案 C）space。downtime 需要 "留白"。其余三项：A）list 错因：list 与 downtime 不搭、B）order 错因："顺序/订单" 与 downtime 无关、D）boundary 错因："边界" 是 "分割" 而非 "留出"，均可排除。
第 16 空正确答案 A）fatigue。social burnout = social ___ 同义替换。其余三项：B）criticism 错因："批评" 与 burnout 不同场、C）injustice 错因："不公正" 与 burnout 无关、D）dilemma 错因："困境" 偏决策，与 burnout 不同向，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 C）signs。列举出的都是 "表现"，不是 "成因"。其余三项：A）sources 错因："来源" 把因果倒置、B）standards 错因："标准" 不合语义、D）scores 错因："得分" 需要量化语境，均可排除。
第 18 空正确答案 D）mark out。下文给出 "留出来的目的"——休息、放松、恢复。其余三项：A）take over 错因："接管" 与 "留时间" 不同义、B）wipe off 错因："擦去" 方向相反、C）add up 错因："累加/合计" 不搭 "日程留时"，均可排除。
第 19 空正确答案 B）unavailable。段意是 "专门划出不社交的时间"。其余三项：A）ungrateful 错因："不感激" 不搭 socialising、C）responsible 错因："对……负责" 方向反、D）regretful 错因："后悔" 是情绪词，与 "是否抽得开身" 无关，均可排除。
第 20 空正确答案 D）rest。三连并列里前后都是 "休/恢复"。其余三项：A）react 错因："反应" 与 "休息" 不同场、B）repeat 错因："重复" 与休息无关、C）return 错因："回归" 单向，且需具体宾语，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Your social life is defined as "the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working". It's important to have a social life, but what's right for one person won't be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, [1] some of us may feel drained, even if it's doing something we enjoy.
paragraphs.zh: 你的社交生活被定义为"当你不工作时，为了娱乐而与他人一起做的活动"。拥有社交生活很重要,但适合一个人的方式不一定适合另一个人。我们中的一些人会因为与他人共度大量时间而感到精力充沛,而我们中的另一些人可能会感到疲惫,即使是在做自己喜欢的事情。

paragraphs.en: This is why finding a [2] in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not [3] others, can make you feel lonely and [4] . Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and [5] a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, [6] , you are working from home and you are [7] on the usual social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes can [8] periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是为什么在社交生活中找到平衡是关键。独自度过太多时间,不与他人见面,会让你感到孤独和疏离。众所周知,孤独会影响你的心理健康并导致情绪低落。任何人在任何时候都可能感到孤独。例如,如果你在家工作,错过了办公室里通常发生的社交对话,这种情况可能尤其真实。其他生活变化也可能引发孤独时期,比如退休、换工作或成为父母。

paragraphs.en: It's important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to [9] a social life, but it can feel overwhelming [10] . It's a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet [11] people. There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to [12] a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and [13] ideas.
paragraphs.zh: 认识到这些孤独感很重要。有一些方法可以重建社交生活,但一开始可能会让人感到难以应对。从思考你喜欢的爱好开始是个好主意。然后你可以找到与这些爱好相关的群体和活动,在那里你将能够遇到志同道合的人。有针对新手父母的群体,针对想首次尝试新运动的人的群体,或者针对同一职业的人聚会和分享想法的社交活动。

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, it's [14] possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you're always doing something and there is never any [15] in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social [16] . We all have our own social limit and it's important to recognise when you're feeling like it's all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be [17] of poor social health. Make sure you [18] some time in your diary when you're [19] for socialising and use this time to relax, [20] and recover.
paragraphs.zh: 另一方面,社交生活也可能过度。如果你觉得自己总是在做某事,日程表上永远没有任何休息时间,你可能会遭受社交倦怠或社交疲劳。我们每个人都有自己的社交极限,重要的是要认识到何时你感觉这一切太多了。情绪低落、精力不足、易怒和睡眠困难都可能是社交健康不良的迹象。确保在你的日程表中标出一些无法参加社交活动的时间,利用这段时间来放松、休息和恢复。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development. But only if you act him out. A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. "The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said. The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been "previously exposed to RSC pedagogy". They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in *The Tempest*. The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage. The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length. They also "appear to be more comfortable writing in role … while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion". The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions". O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful". She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes." The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said. But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".

questions.stem: The "rehearsal room" approach requires pupils to___________.
options: A) rewrite the lines from Shakespeare
C) play the roles in Shakespeare
D) study drama under RSC artists
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 C）play the roles in Shakespeare 定位句在第 2 段：皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC，本研究的委托方）的 Jacqui O'Hanlon 说："这项研究表明，演员的工作方式深深改变了孩子们使用语言的方式，也改变了他们对自己的认识。"正确项与原文构成同义替换（the way actors work ↔ play the roles in Shakespeare；if you act him out ↔ play the roles in Shakespeare）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether___________.
options: A) the change in instruction enhances learning outcomes
B) expanding vocabulary helps develop reading fluency
C) emotion affects understanding of sophisticated works
D) the classroom activity stimulates interest in the arts
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是细节题，正确答案 A）the change in instruction enhances learning outcomes 定位句在第 3 段：他们被分成 target（实验）组和 control（对照）组，被要求以《暴风雨》中船难之后的 Ferdinand 身份写一封”漂流瓶里的信”。target 组额外获得了一个 30 分钟的戏剧化活动来配合该段落。正确项与原文构成同义替换（a 30-minute drama-based activity ↔ the change in instruction；The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length. ↔ enhances learning outcomes）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: Control pupils' reliance on "desert island clichés" shows their ___________.
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是推断题，正确答案 A）weakness in description 定位句在第 5 段："是时候行动"研究还发现：control 组的学生只靠"沙漠岛俗套"（比如棕榈树）来写，而 target 组的学生"更加宏阔，呈现出关于天空、大海与大气状况的更广阔画面"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees ↔ weakness in description；target pupils were "more expansive [giving a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions"]] ↔ weakness in description）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon?
options: A) Writing in an imaginative manner.
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 B）Identifying with literary characters. 定位句在第 6 段：她补充道：“情感理解非常明显，这很可能与”排练室式过程”有关——在那种过程中，你习惯于一路靠想象去走通。他们能从容地描述各种不同的情绪状态，而戏剧的一部分就是把自己放进不同的鞋里（换位）。”正确项与原文构成同义替换（put yourself in different shoes ↔ Identifying with literary characters.；[target children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion]] ↔ Identifying with literary characters.）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、C 项属张冠李戴、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that ___________.
options: A) the new teaching method may work best with Shakespeare
B) the language of Shakespeare may be formidable for pupils
C) other old dramatists may be included in primary education
D) pupils may be reluctant to work on other old dramatists
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是推断题，正确答案 A）the new teaching method may work best with Shakespeare 定位句在第 7 段：但同样的结果换成任何一位老剧作家都能复制吗？O'Hanlon 说还需要更多研究，但暗示莎翁所用 2 万词汇——相较于日常的 2 千词汇——给了”语言进入孩子生活的一次巨大扩展"，再加上孩子"用整个身体把词带活"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? ↔ the new teaching method may work best with Shakespeare；Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives" ↔ the new teaching method may work best with Shakespeare）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属过度推断、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development. But only if you act him out.
paragraphs.zh: 这位来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福的文法学校男孩取得了一次学术上的胜利,突破性研究表明,莎士比亚确实有益于儿童的读写能力和情感发展。但前提是你要把他的作品表演出来。

paragraphs.en: A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. "The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
paragraphs.zh: 一项研究发现,"排练室"式的莎士比亚教学方法拓宽了儿童的词汇量和写作的复杂性,以及他们的情感素养。委托该研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团(RSC)的Jacqui O'Hanlon说:"研究表明,演员的工作方式对儿童使用语言的方式以及他们如何看待自己产生了很大的影响。"

paragraphs.en: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been "previously exposed to RSC pedagogy". They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in *The Tempest*. The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
paragraphs.zh: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所公立小学的数百名9至10岁的五年级学生,这些学校此前"未接触过RSC教学法"。他们被分为目标组和对照组,并被要求完成写作任务,例如在《暴风雨》中船只失事后以Ferdinand的身份写一封漂流瓶信件。目标组获得了30分钟的戏剧活动来配合这段文本。

paragraphs.en: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length. They also "appear to be more comfortable writing in role … while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion".
paragraphs.zh: 经同行评审的结果显示,目标组学生运用了更广泛的词汇,使用了"被归类为更复杂或更罕见"的词语,并且写作篇幅更长。他们还"在角色扮演写作中似乎更加自如……当对照组学生想象自己在遭遇海难时会如何反应时,目标组儿童则设身处地为文学角色着想,并表达该角色的情感"。

paragraphs.en: The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions".
paragraphs.zh: 《该行动的时候了》研究还发现,对照组学生依赖于"荒岛陈词滥调",如棕榈树,而目标组学生则"更具扩展性,对天空、海洋和大气条件给出了更广阔的描绘"。

paragraphs.en: O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful". She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes." The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
paragraphs.zh: O'Hanlon说,最令她惊讶的是目标组"儿童写作中体现出的情感素养",以及他们"在写作中更有韧性,更有希望"。她补充道:"情感理解非常明显,这可能与排练室过程有关,在那里你习惯于尝试通过想象来体验。他们能够自如地描述不同的情感状态,而戏剧的部分工作就是让你设身处地为他人着想。"她说,该研究显示了将艺术融入教育的重要性。

paragraphs.en: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".
paragraphs.zh: 但这些结果能否在任何其他剧作家身上复制呢?O'Hanlon表示需要更多研究,但她指出,莎士比亚使用了20000个词汇,而日常用语只有2000个词汇,这为"儿童生活带来了语言的大规模扩展",并与儿童"用整个身体让词语生动起来"相结合。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions. The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable. It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet's pulse—demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science's unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world's electricity. However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can't track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it's coming from and who's producing it? The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet. It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity's greatest challenges. Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world's solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world's carbon emissions. Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe's largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani. If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.

questions.stem: The author expressed great surprise at some scientists' ________.
options: A) unwillingness to cut carbon emissions
B) intention to reduce their research
D) waste of electricity in their projects
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 B）intention to reduce their research 定位句在第 1 段：我最近吃惊地得知，一些科学家想要缩减他们的科研工作，以求降低碳排放。正确项与原文构成同义替换（scale back their research ↔ reduce their research；some scientists want to ↔ intention to）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author believes that carbon emissions from research ________.
options: C) are hard to handle at present
D) are justifiable in the long run
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 D）are justifiable in the long run 定位句在第 3 段：然而，这是我们为理解世界必须付出的代价。……科技研究产生的碳排放是值得花的：归根到底，这些研究将守护我们星球的未来。正确项与原文构成同义替换（are well spent ↔ are justifiable；ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet ↔ in the long run）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The example of Green in Paragraph 5 is used to illustrate ________.
options: A) the achievements of great scientists
B) the urgency of addressing climate change
C) the rewards of scientific endeavours
D) the value of fostering human ingenuity
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是例证目的题，正确答案 C）the rewards of scientific endeavours 定位句在第 5 段：正是出于对科学与工程所能带来希望的肯定，才有了千禧科技奖的设立；该奖如今已步入第 20 年，意在表彰人类的智慧创造。正确项与原文构成同义替换（was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize ↔ the rewards of scientific endeavours；Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring ↔ the rewards of scientific endeavours）。其余三项中，A 项属答非所问、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last two paragraphs that LUMI ________.
options: A) is a model of sustainability efforts
B) is a triumph against energy shortage
C) owes much to global net-zero initiatives
D) aims to explore the power of intelligence
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是推断题，正确答案 A）is a model of sustainability efforts 定位句在第 6 段：一个绝佳的例子就是欧洲最大的超算——位于芬兰的 LUMI，它令人惊讶地实现了碳负排放。它建在一座旧造纸厂中，由附近的河流供能，其余热则温暖着周边卡亚尼镇的居民。正确项与原文构成同义替换（A great example of this ↔ is a model of sustainability efforts；we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs ↔ is a model of sustainability efforts）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements would the author agree with?
options: A) Emission-free modelling demands extra funding.
B) The need for supercomputers is difficult to meet.
C) Energy-intensive research work is inevitable.
D) The goals of researchers ought to be realistic.
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 C）Energy-intensive research work is inevitable. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（this is a price we must pay for understanding the world ↔ Energy-intensive research work is inevitable；demand significant amounts of energy ↔ Energy-intensive research work is inevitable；The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent ↔ Energy-intensive research work is inevitable）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions. The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
paragraphs.zh: 我最近震惊地得知，一些科学家想要缩减他们的研究以减少碳排放。他们说，危机已经来临，我们需要削减能源密集型的建模工作。至少，我们需要让我们的能源使用变得更加可持续。

paragraphs.en: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet's pulse—demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science's unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world's electricity.
paragraphs.zh: 毋庸置疑的是，我们的实验室、科学仪器、火箭和卫星——这些我们科学家测量地球脉搏所需的工具——在建造和运行过程中都需要大量能源。同样不可否认的是，科学对信息的不懈追求已经导致世界各地能源密集型数据中心的激增。根据国际能源署的数据，这些建筑现在消耗了全球约1%的电力。

paragraphs.en: However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can't track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it's coming from and who's producing it? The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这是我们为了理解世界必须付出的代价。如果我们无法追踪大气中二氧化碳的含量、它的来源以及谁在产生它，我们又如何能向决策者提供关于降低碳排放最佳方式的信息呢？技术研究产生的碳排放是值得的：最终这些研究将保护我们星球的未来。

paragraphs.en: It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity's greatest challenges.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家们可能难以证明这一点，因为我们的工作复杂，通常在闭门进行，而且并不总是容易解释或说明。但是，如果我们要解决人类最大的挑战，展示科学的有效性将至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world's solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world's carbon emissions.
paragraphs.zh: 认识到科学和工程能够带来的希望是创立千年技术奖的动力，该奖项现在进入第20年，作为对人类智慧的庆祝。过去的获奖者之一，来自澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的Martin Green教授，是钝化发射极和背面电池技术的发明者，该技术现在应用于世界上大多数太阳能电池板。多亏了他的发明，我们有了真正的机会来减少世界的碳排放。

paragraphs.en: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe's largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
paragraphs.zh: 每一天，科学家、技术专家和工程师都在发现利用可再生能源的新方法，并开发技术不仅更智能地使用电力，而且为我们的智能提供动力。一个很好的例子是欧洲最大的超级计算机，位于芬兰的LUMI，它惊人地实现了碳负排放。它建立在一座旧造纸厂内，由附近的河流供电，其余热为周围Kajaani镇的居民供暖。

paragraphs.en: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
paragraphs.zh: 如果世界要实现其净零排放的目标，我们必须认真思考如何提供可持续计算并建造更多的LUMI。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions. With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that's working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years. Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce's Global Innovation Policy Center. The global impact is about $71 billion annually. "The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations," says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. "This is organized crime." Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates. ACE says it's helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA's support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyrighted material a serious crime. Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services' cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. "While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline," says analyst Steve Hawley.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, legitimate streaming services ________.
options: A) have drawn lessons from Hollywood
B) have surpassed cable in revenue
D) are confronted with a real threat
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 D）are confronted with a real threat 定位句在第 1 段：自从在 Netflix 的主场上跟它较量起，老牌好莱坞就一直难以在流媒体上盈利，Disney+、Peacock、Paramount+ 等每年亏损数十亿美元，令人担忧这些服务永远赶不上当年有线电视的利润；但流媒体时代倒成全了一些 "意外赢家"——盗版者用软件几秒钟就能从正版在线视频平台上扒下一部电影或电视剧、放到自己的非法网站上播放，每年从广告和订阅里捞约 20 亿美元。正确项与原文构成同义替换（pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions ↔ are confronted with a real threat；has struggled to turn a profit in streaming ↔ are confronted with a real threat）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned that streamers like Netflix ________.
options: A) played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing
B) reaped benefits from the war with digital pirates
C) promised to become big job creators in the US
D) used to collaborate with file-uploading platforms
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是推断题，正确答案 A）played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing 定位句在第 3 段：起初，像 Netflix 这样的合法在线生意的崛起，其实帮助遏制了数字盗版，而当时的盗版主要靠文件上传维系。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads ↔ played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 4 that the MPA ________.
options: A) was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley
B) led a national protest against online piracy
C) was urged to form an enforcement task force
D) failed to win support from local authorities
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是推断题，正确答案 A）was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley 定位句在第 4 段：Rivkin 于 2017 年加入 MPA，此前五年，MPA 曾试图在好莱坞和硅谷之间凝聚共识、推动国会通过一项反在线盗版的立法，但失败了。正确项与原文构成同义替换（failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy ↔ was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Hawley, digital piracy ________.
options: A) cannot be checked in spite of new legislation
B) will possibly overwhelm legitimate streamers
C) is unlikely to diminish in the near future
D) has been underestimated by some analysts
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 C）is unlikely to diminish in the near future 定位句在第 6 段：尽管有人乐观地认为，新的对策与最佳实践或许会让盗版在 2027 年趋于平稳，但各方对于盗版何时开始下降仍无共识。正确项与原文构成同义替换（there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline ↔ is unlikely to diminish in the near future；emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027 ↔ is unlikely to diminish in the near future）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断、B 项属过度推断、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following is emphasized in the text?
options: A) The need to coordinate anti-piracy action.
B) The criminal nature of copyright violation.
C) The prospect of eliminating online piracy.
D) The economic harm from illegal streaming.
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是主旨题，正确答案 D）The economic harm from illegal streaming. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions ↔ The economic harm from illegal streaming.；piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs ↔ The economic harm from illegal streaming.；legitimate US streaming services' cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years ↔ The economic harm from illegal streaming.）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、B 项属以偏概全、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
paragraphs.zh: 自从老好莱坞在Netflix Inc.的地盘上与其竞争以来，一直难以在流媒体业务上实现盈利，Disney+、Peacock和Paramount+等平台每年损失数十亿美元,引发了人们对这些服务可能永远无法像有线电视那样盈利的担忧。但流媒体时代却让一些意想不到的赢家受益:那些使用软件在几秒钟内从合法在线视频平台翻录电影或电视节目,并在自己的非法服务上托管这些内容的盗版者,他们每年通过广告和订阅获得约20亿美元的收入。

paragraphs.en: With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that's working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.
paragraphs.zh: 据代表好莱坞制片厂的行业组织美国电影协会(MPA)称,由于没有视频制作成本,非法流媒体网站的利润率接近90%。该协会正在努力打击近年来出现的数千个非法平台。

paragraphs.en: Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce's Global Innovation Policy Center. The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
paragraphs.zh: 最初,Netflix等合法在线业务的兴起实际上有助于遏制主要基于文件上传的数字盗版。但现在,涉及非法流媒体服务和文件共享的盗版行为每年给美国经济造成约300亿美元的收入损失和约25万个工作岗位的流失,这是美国商会全球创新政策中心的估计。全球影响每年约为710亿美元。

paragraphs.en: "The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations," says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. "This is organized crime." Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
paragraphs.zh: MPA首席执行官Charlie Rivkin说:"那些窃取我们的电影和电视节目并运营盗版网站的人不是夫妻店式的小作坊,这是有组织犯罪。"Rivkin于2017年加入MPA,此前该组织在五年前未能在好莱坞和硅谷之间建立共识,以推动国会通过旨在制止在线盗版的立法。2017年,该协会成立了创意与娱乐联盟(ACE),这是一个由约100名侦探组成的执法特遣队,在全球范围内协助地方当局逮捕流媒体盗版者。

paragraphs.en: ACE says it's helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA's support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyrighted material a serious crime.
paragraphs.zh: ACE表示,在MPA支持2020年联邦法律(该法律将大规模流媒体传播受版权保护的材料定为重罪)的部分帮助下,它已协助将北美的非法流媒体服务数量从2018年的1400多个减少到126个。

paragraphs.en: Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services' cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. "While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline," says analyst Steve Hawley.
paragraphs.zh: 咨询公司Parks Associates预测,自2022年以来,美国合法流媒体服务因盗版造成的累计损失将在未来两年达到1130亿美元。分析师Steve Hawley说:"虽然有一些乐观情绪认为,新兴的对策和最佳实践可能会使盗版在2027年之前开始趋于平稳,但利益相关者对于何时可能开始下降尚未达成共识。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Visit any antiques store and you'll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-65 World's Fair, the ephemera of history. Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible. Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia, we've known what we've known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators' neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on. Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information. Librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems. Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog. Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that's saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog. As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. While future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.

questions.stem: The author mentions the artifacts from the past to ________.
options: A) introduce the collection of antiques
B) contrast them with everyday items
C) bring up the issue of preservation
D) comment on their historical value
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是例证目的题，正确答案 C）bring up the issue of preservation 定位句在第 1 段：然而这些东西并非真正转瞬即逝，因为几十年甚至几百年后它们依然在这里。为什么？因为它们是有形的。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible. ↔ bring up the issue of preservation）。其余三项中，A 项属把例子当主题的典型干扰、B 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts ________.
options: A) are less subject to their creators' neglect
B) convey information in a more direct way
D) are less likely to suffer serious damage
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 B）convey information in a more direct way 定位句在第 2 段：物件本身就是承载并传递信息的媒介。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. ↔ convey information in a more direct way）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, librarians' work may result in ________.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 B）undervaluation of libraries 定位句在第 3 段：图书馆员的无私付出反过来会害了我们——用户举起手机说「一切都在这里」，以此为据声称图书馆对今日的研究者已没那么重要。正确项与原文构成同义替换（libraries are less vital for researchers today ↔ undervaluation of libraries）。其余三项中，A 项属答非所问、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The "ZIP disk" is cited as an example to show ________.
options: A) the hazard of retrieving files through unusual means
B) the infeasibility of constantly migrating digital assets
C) the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats
D) the inconvenience of storing information on analog devices
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是例证目的题，正确答案 C）the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats 定位句在第 4 段：随着技术演进、格式过时，存储物件便变得毫无用处。你是否曾无助地盯着一张 ZIP 盘心想：要怎么把里面的文件取出来？正确项与原文构成同义替换（As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. ↔ the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats；Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? ↔ the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best summarizes the text?

paragraphs.en: Visit any antiques store and you'll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-65 World's Fair, the ephemera of history. Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible.
paragraphs.zh: 走进任何一家古董店,你都会遇到来自过去的物品:照片、信件、一本详细介绍1964至1965年世界博览会Sinclair恐龙展的小册子,这些都是历史的短暂遗存。然而这些物品并非真正短暂,因为它们仍在这里,历经数十年甚至数百年之久。为什么?因为它们是有形的。

paragraphs.en: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia, we've known what we've known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators' neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on. Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information. Librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
paragraphs.zh: 你是否思考过无形格式、数字信息的生命周期,考虑到那些生产这些物品的人很少为其长期保存做准备?几千年来,我们之所以知道我们所知道的,是因为那些留存下来的物品,往往是不顾其最初创造者的疏忽而留存的。物品本身就是传递信息的媒介。在创作之时,并没有进行任何有意的保存尝试,然而模拟材料有机会存活下来,并作为传记作家、历史学家和小说家所依赖的历史记录。图书馆和档案馆传统上承担着组织、保存和提供信息获取的责任。图书管理员将有形物品数字化,以便世界各地的研究人员能够快速搜索和访问他们的馆藏。其结果是历史资源的丰富过剩,这也带来了大海捞针式的问题。

paragraphs.en: Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
paragraphs.zh: 图书管理员的无私奉献可能对我们不利,当用户举起手机说'全都在这里面'来证明图书馆对今天的研究人员不那么重要时,他们以此指向获取的普遍性。然而这种普遍的获取是如何实现的,或许更重要的是,它是如何维护的?谁来策划保存什么?当涉及原生数字信息时,可怕的答案可能是:如果不是图书管理员和档案管理员,那就没有人。数字信息比模拟信息需要多得多的照料。

paragraphs.en: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that's saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog.
paragraphs.zh: 即使数字对象被保存下来,可能只有载体被保存,而不是信息本身。随着技术进步和格式变得过时,该对象就变得毫无用处。你是否曾无助地盯着一张ZIP磁盘,想着:我怎样才能把文件从这里面取出来?如果没有数字资产的持续迁移,一个关于可预见未来的噩梦就是让历史学家夜不能寐的:当数字取代模拟时,历史记录突然中断。

paragraphs.en: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. While future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名日常工作围绕特藏和数字资产的图书管理员,我与历史学家有着同样的夜间恐惧,如果我说目前存在全面的保存解决方案,那我就是在撒谎。然而研究人员可以从一个事实中得到一些安慰,即有众多图书管理员致力于为当前和未来的研究人员发现、组织和保存数字信息。虽然未来的研究人员可能会发现数字领域是一个具有挑战性的工作场所,但他们不会发现它是一个不可能的场所。

paragraphs.zh: Pavlopetri（该遗址的现代名称）位于伯罗奔尼撒半岛南部，约在公元前3500年作为新石器时代定居点出现，后成为迈锡尼希腊（公元前1650-1180年）的重要贸易中心。爱琴海的这一地区易发生地震和海啸，导致该城市逐渐下沉。地中海海平面的缓慢上升使这座城市在3000多年前被淹没。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage. In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems. These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped. Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it. It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand. And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips. The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe. The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today. This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts. Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour. Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers. Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers. To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out. So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation. However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.

Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
paragraphs.zh: 如今的小费要求往往与过去决定何时以及如何支付小费的薪资和服务规范脱节。过去顾客几乎总是在接受服务后支付小费,比如在用完餐后、理完发后或披萨送达后。这种时机可以奖励高质量的服务,并激励员工提供优质服务。

paragraphs.en: It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand. And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
paragraphs.zh: 事先要求支付小费的情况正变得越来越普遍。而新的小费技术甚至可能自动添加小费。

paragraphs.en: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe. The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today. This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
paragraphs.zh: 数字支付设备的普及使向顾客索要小费变得更加容易。这有助于解释为什么小费要求正在渗透到新的服务类型中。顾客现在经常看到建议的默认选项菜单——通常远高于其消费金额的20%。小费金额已从1950年代的10%或更低上升到2000年左右的15%,再到如今的20%或更高。这种增长有时被称为小费通胀——即对越来越高的小费金额的预期。

paragraphs.en: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour. Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
paragraphs.zh: 对于传统上依赖小费的服务行业员工,如餐厅员工,小费一直是重要的收入来源,这些行业的最低小费工资可低至每小时2.13美元。小费蔓延和小费通胀现在进一步补充了许多低薪服务业员工的收入。

paragraphs.en: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers. To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
paragraphs.zh: 值得注意的是,小费主要惠及其中一些员工,如服务员,但不惠及其他员工,如厨师和洗碗工。为确保所有员工获得公平工资,一些餐厅禁止收小费并提高了价格,但这种取消小费服务的运动基本上已经失败。

paragraphs.en: So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation. However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.
paragraphs.zh: 因此,为了在不提高价格的情况下增加员工工资,越来越多的雇主屈服于小费蔓延和小费通胀的诱惑。然而,许多顾客感到沮丧,因为他们觉得自己被要求支付过高的小费,而且频率过高。而且,正如我们的研究所强调的,小费现在似乎更具强制性、更缺乏慷慨性,并且往往与服务质量完全脱节。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served. Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that model is out of date. From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers. With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing out investment in other public services. As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute. Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed. We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it. Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals. And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions. Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims. That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled "Reimagining health", supported by ten former health ministers. Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain. This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than "fix" the NHS. It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes. Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health. Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the heavy price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result. Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system. What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the NHS ________.
options: A) is troubled by funding deficiencies
B) can hardly satisfy people's needs
C) can barely retain its current employees
D) is rivalled by private medical services
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 B）can hardly satisfy people's needs 定位句在第 2 段：在 680 多万人排队候诊的情况下，对于无法选择自费接受私人治疗的人来说，医疗服务正变得越来越难以获得；同时，提供医疗服务的成本正越来越多地挤压对其他公共服务的投入。正确项与原文构成同义替换（healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible ↔ can hardly satisfy people's needs；model is out of date ↔ can hardly satisfy people's needs）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: One answer to the crisis in health and care is to ________.
options: A) boost the efficiency of hospitals
B) lighten the burden on social care
C) increase resources for primary care
D) reduce the pressure on communities
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 C）increase resources for primary care 定位句在第 3 段：我们必须在社区和初级医疗上加大投入，以减少对医院的依赖。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care ↔ increase resources for primary care）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: "Reimagining health" is aimed to ________.
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 C）restructure the health system 定位句在第 4 段：正因如此，Reform 智库正在启动一项名为"重新构想健康"的新工作计划，由十位前卫生大臣支持。我们共同呼吁，就英国健康的未来进行一场更加开放和坦诚的对话，并对我们仍保留的以医院为中心的模式进行一次"紧急重新思考"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain ↔ restructure the health system）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: To maximise the nation's health, the author suggests ________.
options: B) paying due attention to social factors
D) enhancing the quality of healthcare
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 B）paying due attention to social factors 定位句在第 5 段：更重要的是我们居住、工作和社交的场所——然而目前并没有清晰的跨政府战略来改善这些健康的社会决定因素。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise ↔ paying due attention to social factors；these social determinants of health ↔ paying due attention to social factors）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that local leaders should ________.
options: A) exercise their power more reasonably
B) develop a stronger sense of responsibility
C) play a bigger role in the health system
D) understand people's health needs better
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是推断题，正确答案 C）play a bigger role in the health system 定位句在第 6 段：哪些卫生职能应当保留在中央，而哪些应当交给地方负责人——他们往往负责创造健康的相关服务，并对其所辖人群的需求有更为深入的理解？正确项与原文构成同义替换（what should be given to local leaders ↔ play a bigger role in the health system；often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations ↔ play a bigger role in the health system）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断、B 项属无中生有、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served. Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that model is out of date.
paragraphs.zh: 国民健康服务体系(NHS)建立之初颇具远见：提供高质量、及时的医疗服务以满足其所服务人群的主要需求。近75年过去了,英国面临着截然不同的健康挑战,这一模式显然已经过时。

paragraphs.en: From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers. With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing out investment in other public services. As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.
paragraphs.zh: 从预期寿命到癌症和婴儿死亡率,我们都落后于许多同类国家。超过680万人在候诊名单上,医疗服务对那些无力选择支付私人治疗费用的人来说越来越难以获得;提供医疗服务的成本也日益挤压其他公共服务的投资。随着医疗需求持续增长,本已接近崩溃边缘的医疗队伍所面临的压力只会变得更加严峻。

paragraphs.en: Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed. We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it. Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals. And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 解决健康和护理危机的许多答案都已被反复讨论。我们需要在减少和分流医疗服务需求方面做得更好,而不是仅仅对其进行管理。需要在社区和基层医疗方面投入更多资金,以减少我们对医院的依赖。社会护理的能力需要更大,以支持日益增长的长期病患者数量。

paragraphs.en: Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims. That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled "Reimagining health", supported by ten former health ministers. Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,尽管经历了二十年的战略规划和多次重大卫生改革,我们在任何这些目标上都未能取得实质性进展。这就是为什么Reform智库在十位前卫生大臣的支持下启动了一项名为"重新构想健康"的新工作计划。我们共同呼吁就英国健康的未来进行更加开放和诚实的对话,并"紧急反思"我们所保留的以医院为中心的模式。

paragraphs.en: This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than "fix" the NHS. It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes. Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health. Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the heavy price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.
paragraphs.zh: 这必须从如何最大化国民健康这一问题开始,而不是"修复"NHS。例如,据估计,医疗服务仅占健康结果的约20%。更重要的是我们生活、工作和社交的场所——然而政府并没有明确的跨部门战略来改善这些健康的社会决定因素。更糟糕的是,当像国家肥胖战略这样的政策被废弃时,纳税人就要承担治疗由此导致的疾病(如糖尿病)的沉重代价。

paragraphs.en: Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system. What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?
paragraphs.zh: Reform希望探讨权力和资源应该如何在我们的卫生系统中分配。哪些卫生职能应该保留在中央,哪些应该交给地方领导者——他们通常负责创造健康的服务,并且对其人群的需求有更好的了解?

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years. In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions. Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days. But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research. Many lack adequate funding, it found. And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate. In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts. But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs. Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say. That day's high temperature of roughly 36°C was 1°C shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities. But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony. To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions. Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk. Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says. "A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters." For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers. The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer. HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler. In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade. HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations. "Reducing deaths in an emergency is a good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandni Singh.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Nagpur's plan proposes measures to ________.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 A）tackle extreme weather 定位句在第 1 段：比如 Nagpur 的方案要求医院在夏天专门预留「冷病房」以救治中暑患者，并建议建筑商在极热天让建筑工人停工休息。正确项与原文构成同义替换（on very hot days ↔ extreme weather；treating heatstroke patients ↔ tackle）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: One problem with existing HAPs is that they ________.
options: A) prove too costly to be implemented
C) give delayed responses to heat waves
D) keep hospitals under great pressure
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是细节题，正确答案 B）lack localized alert-issuing criteria 定位句在第 2 段：并且，它们的触发阈值常常没有根据当地气候进行定制。正确项与原文构成同义替换（triggering thresholds ↔ alert-issuing criteria；are not customized to the local climate ↔ lack localized）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: Mumbai's case shows that India's heat alert systems need to ________.
options: A) include other factors besides temperature
B) take subtle weather changes into account
C) prioritize potentially disastrous heat waves
D) draw further support from local authorities
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 A）include other factors besides temperature 定位句在第 3 段：但高温的影响被湿度（这是高温预警系统中常被忽视的一个因素）和上午晚些时候户外仪式上缺乏遮蔽放大了。正确项与原文构成同义替换（humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems ↔ other factors besides temperature；often neglected factor ↔ include）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Kotharkar holds that a vulnerability map can help ________.
options: A) prevent the harm of high humidity
B) target areas needing special attention
C) expand the Nagpur project's coverage
D) make relief plans for heat-stricken people
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 B）target areas needing special attention 定位句在第 5 段：比如，老年人口多或难以抵御高温的非正式住宅集中的社区，可获得专项预警或被加强配备冷却中心。Nagpur 项目已建立了一份风险与脆弱性地图，让 Kotharkar 能告诉官员热浪来临时应重点关注哪些社区。正确项与原文构成同义替换（which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave ↔ target areas needing special attention；focus responses on the populations most at risk ↔ areas needing special attention）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, researchers believe that HAPs should ________.
options: A) focus more on heatstroke treatment
B) apply for more government grants
D) serve a broader range of purposes
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是细节题，正确答案 D）serve a broader range of purposes 定位句在第 6 段：研究人员表示，HAPs 不应只包含短期应急响应，还应推荐能让社区更凉爽的中长期措施。正确项与原文构成同义替换（shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures ↔ serve a broader range of purposes；Reducing deaths in an emergency is a good target to have, but it's the lowest target ↔ a broader range of purposes）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years. In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions. Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，高温行动计划(HAPs)在印度迅速普及。一般来说，高温行动计划明确规定了官员应何时以及如何发布高温警报并提醒医院和其他机构。例如,那格浦尔的计划要求医院在夏季预留"降温病房"用于治疗中暑患者,并建议建筑商在酷热天气让建筑工人停工休息。

paragraphs.en: But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research. Many lack adequate funding, it found. And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate. In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts. But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.
paragraphs.zh: 但根据政策研究中心的一份报告,现有高温行动计划的实施情况参差不齐。报告发现,许多计划缺乏充足的资金。而且它们的触发阈值往往没有根据当地气候进行定制。在某些地区,仅白天的高温就可以作为发布警报的充分触发条件。但在其他地方,夜间温度或湿度可能与白天高温一样,都是风险的重要衡量指标。

paragraphs.en: Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say. That day's high temperature of roughly 36°C was 1°C shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities. But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,孟买四月份的中暑死亡事件凸显了制定更细致和本地化预警的必要性。当天约36°C的最高气温比国家气象部门为沿海城市设定的热浪警报阈值低1°C。但高温的影响因湿度而被放大——这是高温警报系统中经常被忽视的因素——以及上午晚些时候户外仪式缺乏遮阴。

paragraphs.en: To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions. Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.
paragraphs.zh: 为了帮助改进高温行动计划,城市规划师Rajashree Kotharkar的团队正在制定一个示范计划,概述最佳实践并可根据当地条件进行调整。她说,除其他事项外,所有城市都应该绘制脆弱性地图,以帮助将应对措施集中在风险最高的人群上。

paragraphs.en: Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says. "A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters." For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers. The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.
paragraphs.zh: Kotharkar说,这种地图绘制不需要很复杂。"只需查看几个关键参数就可以创建一张有用的地图。"例如,老年人口较多或非正式住所不能很好应对高温的社区可以获得特别警报或通过设立降温中心得到加强。那格浦尔项目已经创建了一张风险和脆弱性地图,这使Kotharkar能够告诉官员在今年夏季发生热浪时应关注哪些社区。

paragraphs.en: HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler. In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade. HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations. "Reducing deaths in an emergency is a good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandni Singh.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,高温行动计划不应仅包括短期应急响应,还应推荐可使社区更凉爽的中长期措施。例如在那格浦尔,Kotharkar的团队已能够就在哪里种植树木以提供遮阴向市政官员提供建议。高温行动计划还可以指导房屋改造或修改建筑法规的工作。气候研究员Chandni Singh说:"在紧急情况下减少死亡是一个值得追求的目标,但这是最低目标。

reading.passage: Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parks of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans. Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively. Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour. Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established. Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily, aesthetics. A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks. This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment. The Wickquasgeck Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly. This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street. Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway. Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city. In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub. Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes. Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences. As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.

paragraphs.zh: 因此,下次你需要寻求帮助时,请记住所有这些。同时要注意你向谁求助以及何时求助。如果有人现在无法提供帮助,不要往心里去。他们可能只是太忙了,或者他们可能对自己提供帮助的能力不够自信。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward. They've helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world. But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery. Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa — about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses. The team published their findings in the journal Science this month. "Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves," co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement. "We usually only get the human's side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened. Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived." The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe. They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago. The team reconstructed the animals' evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses. They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later. Though it's still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News' Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier. "Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at crossing deserts," co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabatier University in France, tells the publication. Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help navigate the expanding Sahara. Researchers say these findings could help put donkeys in the spotlight. The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa. But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys. Not only does understanding the equines' genetic makeup help reveal their contribution to human history, but it also might improve their management in the future, as climate change alters the planet's environment, write the authors.

questions.stem: What can be learned about donkeys from Paragraph 1?

B) They underwent multiple domestication events.
C) They were tamed at an earlier time than horses.

B) survived with the help of herders.
D) adapted to the changing environment.
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 A）dispersed widely in the world. 定位句在第 3 段：随后他们追踪了动物如何在约 2500 年后向非洲其他地区扩散，并进入欧洲与亚洲。正确项与原文构成同义替换（spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia ↔ dispersed widely in the world）。其余三项中，B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 B）provides a possible explanation. 定位句在第 4 段：「驴在驮物方面是冠军，且擅长穿越沙漠」，合作者、法国保罗·萨巴蒂耶大学进化生物学家 Orlando 告诉该刊。史前人类可能驯化驴是为了帮助穿越扩张中的撒哈拉。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help navigate the expanding Sahara ↔ provides a possible explanation；Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at crossing deserts ↔ provides a possible explanation）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The authors think that their research could help with ____

paragraphs.en: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward. They've helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world. Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa — about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses. The team published their findings in the journal Science this month.
paragraphs.zh: 数千年来，驴对于推动人类文明前进至关重要。它们帮助拉动轮式车辆，载运旅行者，并在世界各地运输货物。但这些动物最初在何时何地与人类交织在一起一直是个谜。现在，研究人员利用200多头驴的基因组，将它们的驯化追溯到大约7000年前东非的一次单一事件——比人类驯服马匹早约3000年。该团队本月在《科学》杂志上发表了他们的研究结果。

"We usually only get the human's side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened. Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived."
paragraphs.zh: 佛罗里达大学马科动物研究员、共同作者Samantha Brooks在一份声明中说："通过它们的DNA，这些动物正在讲述自己的历史。我们通常只能通过书面记载了解人类一方的历史，但书面历史当然并不总是准确记录事情是如何发生的。通过观察这些DNA序列,我们获得了关于这些动物生活环境和它们经历的生物学证词。

paragraphs.en: The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe. They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago. The team reconstructed the animals' evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses. They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员检查了来自全球31个国家的207个现代驴基因组。他们还研究了15个野生马科动物和31头生活在大约4000年至100年前的早期驴的基因组。该团队重建了这些动物的进化树,并使用计算机模型精确定位了肯尼亚和非洲之角的牧民驯化野驴的驯化事件。然后他们追踪了这些动物如何在大约2500年后传播到非洲其他地区、欧洲和亚洲。

paragraphs.en: Though it's still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News' Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier. "Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at crossing deserts," co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabatier University in France, tells the publication. paragraphs.zh: 尽管最初驯化发生的原因仍不清楚,《科学新闻》的Freda Kreier报道称,该事件与撒哈拉沙漠变得更大更干燥的时期相吻合。法国保罗·萨巴蒂埃大学进化生物学家、共同作者Ludovic Orlando告诉该刊物:"驴在运载物品方面是冠军,而且擅长穿越沙漠。"史前人类可能驯化了驴来帮助穿越不断扩大的撒哈拉沙漠。

The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa. But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,这些发现可能有助于让驴受到关注。这些动物可以从更多研究中受益:目前,没有已发表的来自非洲赤道以南地区驴的基因组。但了解这些动物最初在哪里被驯化,可以引导考古学家在一个狭窄的区域内寻找关于最初驯化的驴的见解。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: There's no business like show business — but in Los Angeles, it feels like there's no business at all. If that sounds melodramatic, consider this: The Art Directors Guild, a labor union representing about 3,000 film workers, has suspended a training program and issued a statement explaining that "we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession." This is a reaction to Hollywood's decline, which is reaching a critical point for the industry and Southern California. Production has been slipping away from Hollywood since the 1950s, but the effects have never been more apparent than at present. Other regions in the United States, Canada and Europe have steadily increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies, leaving California in the dust. Georgia offers up to 30% in transferable tax credits on film and TV production costs, plus an additional 10% increase on the base tax credit if the project includes a Georgia promotional logo. Even as California lost a huge volume of production to other locations, there was still plenty of film production taking place in Los Angeles before this year. We were kept afloat by "peak TV", the glut of content that was required by the explosion of streaming services. But 2022 was the peak of peak TV. Back then platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Apple TV hemorrhaged billions of dollars to generate content to attract new subscribers, resulting in 633 scripted series being released that year. As the streamers' emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability, prices for the services went up and the number of new shows went down to 481 released in 2023, with the number expected to dip into the 300s within a few years. If productions in Southern California dip below a critical level for too long, the industry's essential talent will drift away along with enormous sums of revenue. Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn't offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses that support the entertainment industry. That's why the California Film Commission and its Los Angeles counterpart, Film LA, now should act, before it's too late. These agencies and other government bodies should dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles. Let's go on with the show…and make sure the show doesn't go on without us.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 6, California's entertainment industry might face ____

questions.stem: The author concludes the text by emphasizing that California should strive to ____
